papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line, System‑Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as a core, first‑line strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students when the method is applied as part of a system‑level pipeline. KD reliably reduces inference cost and model size while retaining much of a teacher’s performance across vision, speech, and language tasks, provided practitioners attend to what form of knowledge is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how distillation is combined with structural compression and data strategies. KD’s strengths are its methodological flexibility (soft targets, feature and attention matching, multi‑teacher schedules, and data synthesis) and its ability to compose with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Its principal limits arise from teacher–student mismatch, limited or private data, and risks of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors; these require explicit remedies (capacity-aware student design, representation projection, multi‑teacher or synthetic data, and robustness evaluation). When deployed as an engineering pipeline rather than a single loss term, KD yields compact models that meet practical latency, memory, and deployment constraints while exposing clear research challenges around robustness, privacy, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Patterns, Practical Guidance, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A range of mechanisms—soft-target matching, feature and attention imitation, layer- or module-level mappings, and self- or multi-teacher schemes—enable compact models that often retain much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy. Practical pipelines combine KD with architecture-aware design, pretraining or warming strategies, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization) to meet deployment constraints. However, distillation success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and the choice of distilled signals; important open problems include robust cross-domain transfer, distillation without original data, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors in language tasks, and avoiding transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, cheaper students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, methods range from classic teacher-student logits supervision to data-free and online schemes, meta-learned teachers, and representation-level transfers. Empirical work shows KD often yields substantial efficiency gains but its effectiveness depends on dataset complexity, model capacity, data availability, and optimization choices; important failure modes and practical remediation strategies have been identified.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Mechanisms, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely used approach to compressing large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods span soft-logit matching, ensemble distillation, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, self- and multi-teacher schedules, and privacy- or data-aware variants. Empirical results across vision and language tasks show that carefully chosen distillation targets and student–teacher alignment can achieve large reductions in inference cost with modest loss (and sometimes gains) in performance. However, practical success depends on capacity-matching, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of failure modes such as propagation of teacher errors, degraded rare-token behavior in NLP, and privacy concerns. KD performs best as a component of a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture choices, pruning/quantization, and data-centric strategies.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has matured from simple logits-matching into a multifaceted toolkit that includes soft-target supervision, intermediate representation alignment, attention and relation matching, data synthesis for data-free scenarios, online and federated distillation, and self-distillation. Empirical results show distilled students often approach teacher performance while yielding substantial gains in latency, memory, and deployability; however, practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and mitigation of risks such as bias transfer, robustness loss, and privacy leakage. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative variants, theoretical insights, practical strategies, and open challenges to guide research and deployments in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical, flexible route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining a large fraction of teacher performance. KD spans multiple mechanisms — soft-target matching, intermediate-representation transfer, layer-wise or progressive replacement, privacy- and data-aware variants — and can be combined with structural compression such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is highly effective in many realistic settings but is not universally sufficient: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, what form of knowledge is transferred, data availability (including few-shot or privacy-constrained scenarios), and careful optimization and evaluation. Viewed as a central yet context-sensitive tool, KD should be a default component of compression pipelines, applied in concert with complementary methods and guarded by targeted diagnostics for robustness and rare-token or out-of-distribution behavior.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical, flexible pathway to compress large models into compact, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive power. When combined with complementary techniques (pre-training, layer alignment, architecture-aware design, and data strategies), KD produces efficient models suitable for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings across modalities. This paper argues that KD should be a primary tool in compression pipelines and provides concrete, evidence-based prescriptions and caveats for practitioners.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: The Practical Centrality of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing modern deep models across modalities. When combined with architecture-aware transformations, feature-level supervision, multi-teacher signals, and careful handling of data constraints, KD enables compact students that retain most of a teacher's effectiveness while meeting latency, memory, and domain requirements. However, distillation artifacts and data limitations require methodic choices—e.g., feature mimicking, confidence-aware multi-teacher weighting, or generative replay—to avoid propagating teacher errors or overfitting in low-data regimes.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost while retaining performance. A broad family of approaches—from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free synthesis, and federated or privacy-aware protocols—enables deployment across vision, speech, and language tasks. Practical success depends on matching the distillation signal to student capacity, combining KD with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, pretraining), and addressing data, optimization, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field has matured into a suite of complementary techniques — logits matching, feature and attention imitation, multi-teacher schedules, self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search — and is applied across NLP, vision, speech, multimodal, and specialized domains. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can recover most teacher performance and enable deployment under strict compute, memory, latency, and privacy constraints, but practical success depends on adapting objectives, data strategies, and student architectures to task and deployment constraints. Key open problems include distillation under data heterogeneity and privacy, preserving rare-token fidelity for sequence tasks, transferring robustness, and automating student architectures for diverse tasks.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high‑performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring useful information from teachers. Techniques vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), how teachers are chosen or ensembled, and whether distillation is done with or without access to original data. Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture design, data augmentation, or synthetic-data generation) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often preserves much of teacher performance, success depends on careful objective design, alignment of teacher and student capacity, data strategies, and mitigation of failure modes such as degraded handling of low‑frequency tokens, adversarial vulnerability, or erased relative class information.

papers_seen.author: Gates
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Variants, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a practical, multipurpose toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring information at the output level (soft targets) and across intermediate representations, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of teacher performance. KD is most effective when treated as part of a broader compression strategy that aligns distillation signals to student capacity, leverages data-aware or data-free variants when needed, and combines distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture redesign. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality, data availability and match, and careful choice of what and how to transfer; open problems include preserving rare behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and principled automation of trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used approach to compress large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring useful information from a trained teacher. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a family of techniques that include feature- and attention-level imitation, progressive module replacement, self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. Empirical work across computer vision, ranking, speech, and natural language tasks shows distilled models can approach teacher performance when distillation is matched to student capacity, task demands, and data availability. Practical deployment requires combining KD with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and fairness/privacy safeguards while managing trade-offs between fidelity, robustness, and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context‑Dependent Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied deliberately—choosing which teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity and inputs, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques—KD routinely delivers large reductions in model size and latency while preserving most task performance. Real-world success requires representation-aware objectives, options for data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings, and careful evaluation under distribution shift and modality-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Practice, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, practical toolkit for producing compact, faster models from large neural teachers in deep learning and NLP. KD methods extend beyond soft-target matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free strategies. In practice, distillation is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization); careful choice of what to transfer, how to align layers, and what data to use is critical. Remaining challenges include reliably preserving rare-token behavior, robustness and fairness under compression, data-free and privacy-preserving distillation, and principled co-design of teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression methods transfer knowledge from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving performance. Approaches span soft-label (logit) matching, feature- or attention-level imitation, multi-teacher fusion, data-free distillation, and adaptations for domain shift and heterogeneous deployment. Empirical results show distilled students can approach or match teacher performance in many settings, but success depends on teacher quality, the form of transferred knowledge, training curricula, and application-specific design choices. Emerging theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and reveal practical tradeoffs such as bias–variance effects of soft labels and the roles of ensemble and self-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques seek to reduce the runtime, memory, and deployment costs of large deep models while retaining their predictive performance or improving other desiderata (e.g., interpretability, fairness). Across vision and language domains, methods range from classical teacher-to-student soft-target distillation to transferring intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, selective sample-driven distillation, and teacher-adaptive or teacher-free schemes. Empirical work shows that carefully chosen distillation targets, alignment of intermediate representations, and input-side practices (such as tailored data augmentation) can materially affect student performance. Remaining challenges include representation mismatches between teacher and student, identifying which training samples are beneficial for transfer, and adapting distillation to domain- or resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression approaches transfer information from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, deployable students or otherwise reduce model complexity while preserving task performance. Across vision and NLP, practitioners use a range of supervision signals and training protocols—soft-target matching, feature and attention imitation, representation-level objectives, self-distillation, online co-training, and data-free generation—to trade off accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Empirical work shows that carefully chosen distillation signals and training recipes can produce compact models that approach teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, data availability, and alignment between teacher signals and downstream tasks. Open challenges include robust transfer of rare-token behavior, principled selection of what to distill, and scaling distillation to privacy-sensitive or distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective strategy for compressing large models into efficient students across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains. Beyond simply matching teacher logits, modern KD benefits from teaching intermediate representations, mimicking teacher features, self-distillation, and careful handling of multiple or stronger teachers. KD also composes well with structured pruning and other compression techniques to meet hardware constraints. This article synthesizes empirical lessons and recommended practices for applying KD reliably in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical family of methods for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Over the past decade KD has evolved from soft-target (logit) matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schedules, data-free or synthetic-data approaches, and teacher-free/self-distillation variants. KD is most effective when treated as a system-level design choice—selecting appropriate distillation signals, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. While KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost with modest performance loss, its success depends on data availability, optimization dynamics, teacher quality, and careful evaluation of robustness and fairness; open challenges remain around domain shift, preserving rare-token behaviors in language models, privacy-aware distillation, and principled data-free methods.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are a widely adopted toolkit for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the accuracy of larger teachers. Research across vision and language characterizes KD as a family of methods—transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training signals via specialized curricula or online exchanges—and shows that KD integrates naturally with pretraining, architecture design, and deployment-aware strategies. Practical success depends on matching the choice of knowledge (what to transfer), the teacher-student pairing (capacity and architecture), available data (real, augmented, or synthetic), and optimization curricula to the target task and constraints. While KD routinely yields substantial runtime and memory gains with modest accuracy loss, open challenges remain in handling domain shift, rare-token transfer in NLP, optimization mismatch, and large-scale or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of methods that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models so deployments meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate-representation and attention matching, relational or structural transfer, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-side interventions (including data-free and few-shot protocols). When combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and appropriate data and optimization practices, KD yields compact models that recover a large fraction of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. Open problems include principled theory of when KD helps, reliably transferring robustness and fairness, handling distribution shift and rare or low-frequency phenomena in NLP, and automated student design under strict resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring useful predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, KD variants—ranging from soft-target matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware approaches—enable substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data and augmentation strategies, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, low-precision numerics). When these components are co-designed, distilled models can approach teacher-level performance and support real-world, resource-constrained deployments, though open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, rare-token fidelity, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become practical tools to reduce model size and computation while retaining much of the performance of large teachers. Across vision, speech, and natural language tasks, approaches include transferring soft logits, mimicking internal features or attention maps, layering/structural adaptations, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or privacy-preserving methods. Empirical results demonstrate that careful distillation can yield compact students that approach teacher accuracy and enable deployment in resource-constrained settings, but open challenges remain in robustness, task-specific distillation design, and distributed training dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques that transfer information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals), how data are used or synthesized, and how training is scheduled (offline, online, self-distillation, adversarial compression). Empirical work shows KD can enable deployable models across vision, speech, and NLP, but success depends on aligning teacher-student inputs and representations, addressing optimization mismatches, and adapting objectives to task and data constraints. Open challenges include data-free distillation, cross-domain generalization, robustness, fairness, and principled choices of distillation targets for heterogeneous student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transform large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster, and more deployable models while attempting to preserve accuracy and useful inductive biases. Approaches span classic teacher–student logit matching, representation and feature imitation, layer mapping strategies for large pretrained language models, data-free and zero-shot methods that avoid access to original training data, and privacy- or communication-aware frameworks for distributed settings. Empirical work demonstrates these methods can yield practical speedups, substantial parameter reductions, and competitive task performance across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks; theoretical and empirical studies also clarify when softened teacher targets or distilled datasets best help student capacity. Remaining challenges include balancing privacy and utility, reducing the cost of distillation when teachers are large, and extending guarantees and methods across modalities and domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Multi-purpose Strategy for Model Compression and Robust Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving or even improving task performance. Beyond simple size reduction, KD supports domain adaptation, latency-aware architecture transformations, robustness transfer, and interpretable model surrogates. When combined with careful training protocols (e.g., multi-teacher schemes, domain adaptation, or targeted regularization), distillation enables deployment of high-performing models in resource- and latency-constrained or safety-critical settings across vision, speech, 3D perception, and natural language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Powerful but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity and inputs, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD routinely reduces model size and latency while preserving much task performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-specific phenomena (e.g., rare-token behavior), so careful protocol design and evaluation under realistic constraints are essential.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models so that high-performing systems can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure; they can be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture-design choices to meet hardware and application requirements. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance and can improve student generalization, but outcomes depend on what is distilled, teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free or federated settings), and optimization choices. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a flexible component in a broader compression strategy and adapt distillation signals, data strategies, and student architectures to the target deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Multifaceted, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central practical technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their predictive power. When combined with complementary strategies—task-aware objectives, intermediate representation matching, online or distributed schemes, and teacher-student co-design—KD supports deployment on resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive environments. Nonetheless, its effectiveness depends strongly on teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability (including few-shot or data-free regimes), and the choice of distilled signals; recognizing these dependencies leads to principled best practices that balance fidelity, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of model-compression techniques that trains smaller student models to reproduce useful behavior from larger teacher models. Across vision and language tasks, KD methods extend beyond matching soft teacher outputs to include alignment of internal representations, attention or relational signals, adversarially-informed objectives, online or multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware strategies. Effective application balances what is transferred, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and robustness or fairness constraints, and it is typically combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, often ensemble or higher-capacity teacher models to smaller student models to improve accuracy, robustness, interpretability, or resource efficiency. Over the past decade KD has been adapted beyond the original soft-label logits transfer: methods now target intermediate features, attention maps, channel-wise signals, and training curricula; they address deployment constraints such as low-precision arithmetic, absence of original data, heterogeneous device models, and federated settings. In NLP, distillation has been applied to compress pretrained language models, to enable multi-task or lifelong learning, and to improve robustness in tasks such as question answering and machine translation. Practical recipes combine architectural adjustments, selective or staged distillation, and application-specific modifications to retain teacher strengths while avoiding transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a single compression trick but a flexible set of techniques that can reduce model size, preserve or transfer task-relevant information, enable deployment in latency- and memory-constrained settings, support domain adaptation and privacy-preserving federated workflows, and be combined with structural compression. When applied thoughtfully — with task-aware selection of distilled signals, architecturally informed teacher-student design, and attention to data availability and optimization dynamics — KD yields large practical benefits for deep learning and NLP systems while avoiding common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher performance. KD operates at multiple levels — softened output distributions, intermediate feature or attention imitation, and relational or layer-wise alignment — and composes naturally with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD yields substantial gains in latency, memory, and energy for deployed systems, but its success depends on careful design choices related to what is distilled, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and robustness or fairness requirements. Practical deployment treats KD as a core element of a hybrid compression pipeline, with task-aware signal selection, student-aware teacher design, and targeted remedies for distribution shift, low-frequency phenomena, adversarial vulnerability, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, distillation variants — from logits matching to internal representation transfer, data-free synthesis, online peer-teaching, and AutoML-guided student search — enable deployment under tight latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When combined with task-aware design, multi-teacher curricula, and safeguards for fairness and privacy, KD yields compact models that meet real-world production requirements while preserving most of the teacher’s utility.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Challenges, and Empirical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a diverse set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Approaches extend beyond matching soft logits to include intermediate-feature mimicry, attention-driven layer alignment, many-to-many layer mapping, contrastive representation alignment, and task- or domain-aware search and adaptation. Empirical work shows KD is effective across modalities and tasks — from pre-trained language models and visual-linguistic systems to object detectors, recommender rankers, graph networks, and continual learning settings — but practical deployment requires addressing representation misalignment, task specificity, and catastrophic forgetting. This review synthesizes core strategies and key empirical findings to guide application and future research.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Toward Representation- and Strategy-driven Knowledge Distillation for Efficient and Robust NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation remains a central approach to compress large deep learning models for deployment in resource-constrained and domain-specific NLP settings. I argue that to realize reliably compact and generalizable student models we must move past sole reliance on teacher soft-labels and adopt representation-aware objectives, structured channel/feature matching, adaptive training curricula, and practical strategies for low-precision, data-limited, and privacy-sensitive scenarios. Combining these approaches yields students that better capture teacher knowledge, adapt to new domains, and meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to what knowledge is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), how teachers and students are aligned, and how data (real, synthetic, or absent) are handled, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when practitioners explicitly address robustness, fairness, and distributional mismatch. However, KD is context-dependent: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and the choice of distillation signal determine success, and careful objective design and evaluation are required to avoid propagating teacher errors or amplifying undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from teacher models. KD encompasses a family of techniques — matching teacher logits (soft targets), aligning intermediate features or attention maps, online or mutual distillation, self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware variants — that are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance in vision and language tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality and specialization, student capacity and architecture, availability and alignment of data, and optimization choices; naive distillation can propagate teacher errors or fail under strong teacher–student mismatch. Practical pipelines therefore select distillation signals and schedules appropriate to task and deployment constraints, often pairing KD with complementary compression techniques to trade compute and size for modest predictive degradation.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques that transfer information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals), how data are used or synthesized, and how training is scheduled (offline, online, self-distillation, adversarial compression). Empirical work shows KD can enable deployable models across vision, speech, and NLP, but success depends on aligning teacher-student inputs and representations, addressing optimization mismatches, and adapting objectives to task and data constraints. Open challenges include data-free distillation, cross-domain generalization, robustness, fairness, and principled choices of distillation targets for heterogeneous student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has evolved from matching softened logits to a broad family of methods that include intermediate-feature alignment, attention- and relation-based transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, data-free or synthetic-data strategies, and architecture-aware compression. Practically, KD enables favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks but requires careful design around the form of knowledge transferred, teacher–student compatibility, data availability and augmentation, and evaluation for robustness and undesired behavior. Open problems remain in reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors in sequence tasks, and ensuring fairness and robustness in deployed compact models.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: The Versatility and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students while preserving much of their performance. Across domains — including reinforcement learning, vision, generative modeling, and language — distillation can accelerate inference, enable deployment on constrained devices, and transfer capabilities such as domain adaptation or lifelong learning. However, its effectiveness depends on choices about teacher-student pairing, data availability and augmentation, sample selection, and training protocols; it also interacts with privacy and heterogeneity constraints. A balanced approach that combines principled distillation objectives, appropriate data strategies (including data-free methods when necessary), and curriculum or annealing schedules yields the best tradeoffs between compactness and retained performance.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models by transferring information from high-capacity teachers to smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while retaining much of the teacher performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded from logits-based soft-target matching to a rich family of techniques including feature- and attention-level alignment, relational and representation matching, student-aware teacher design, and integration with architecture search and other compression primitives. Empirical work across vision and language shows KD both as a route to practical deployment of pre-trained transformers and as a general regularizer that can improve student generalization; ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous architectures, coping with limited or private data, and preserving performance on rare classes or tokens. This article synthesizes core methods, mechanistic explanations, practical adaptations for NLP, and directions where KD currently has the greatest impact.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile family of techniques for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across vision and language, KD variants—ranging from softened-logit transfer to intermediate-feature mimicry, attention matching, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and task-aware architecture search—enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and applied with careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data handling, and training curricula, KD routinely delivers large reductions in model size and inference cost while keeping accuracy losses modest. Nonetheless, KD is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on the choice of transferred signals, training data availability, teacher quality, and explicit checks for robustness and distribution shift. Practical adoption requires co-design of teacher and student, selection of appropriate distillation objectives, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Work across vision and language shows a set of recurring strategies: transfer using softened outputs (soft targets), imitation of intermediate/internal representations, layer mapping between teacher and student, task-adaptive architecture search, self-distillation, and data-free distillation when original training data are unavailable. Empirical results indicate that properly designed distillation can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while offering large gains in inference speed and memory; however, success depends on which knowledge is transferred (outputs vs. internal features), how layers are aligned, and whether task specificity and data availability are addressed. The field currently balances practical engineering (architecture and search) with algorithmic refinements (losses and training regimes), and open challenges include robust data-free methods, principled many-to-many layer matching, and teacher designs that are optimized to be “student-friendly.”

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. A broad family of KD methods transfers teacher behavior through soft-label matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention- or task-aware layer projection, ensemble/online schemes, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols. When combined with architecture search, progressive module replacement, or data synthesis, KD enables strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs that make large pretrained models practical for edge, federated, and privacy-sensitive deployments. Key practical decisions include what form of knowledge to transfer, how to align mismatched teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or no access to original training data. Remaining challenges center on teacher–student compatibility, data heterogeneity, robustness under compression, and principled selection of distilled signals for downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compact, High-Quality Models in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models for deployment. Across NLP and other modalities, distillation enables lightweight architectures to retain much of a teacher's performance while supporting additional compression techniques (pruning, quantization) and privacy-respecting or data-free workflows. However, distillation outcomes depend strongly on teacher–student compatibility, the form of distilled knowledge (logits, features, attention), access to data, and optimization choices. Best results arise when distillation is integrated with appropriate pre-training, architectural adapters (projectors or attention alignment), and, when necessary, data synthesis or domain adaptation.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Primary, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When applied thoughtfully—choosing appropriate distillation signals (logits, features, attention), accounting for teacher–student capacity, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—KD reliably reduces memory, compute, and latency burdens while enabling deployment across edge, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. However, KD is not a universal cure: its benefits depend on optimization, data availability, and robustness/fairness goals, and practical deployments require matching KD variants to constraints and verifying student behavior under distribution shift and adversarial threats.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central Tool for Practical Model Compression, with Limits and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. When combined with complementary strategies—such as intermediate-feature alignment, architecture-aware design, data-aware selection, and data-free synthesis—distillation enables practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. However, KD is not universally sufficient: careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data or domain mismatch is required to avoid propagating errors or losing robustness.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A diverse set of KD mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, attention- and relation-based signals, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data synthesis—has been developed and combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance in many vision and language tasks, while remaining sensitive to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, domain shift, and robustness concerns. Practical pipelines therefore co-design student architectures, distillation targets, and data handling strategies to achieve the best trade-offs for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line, System‑Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models that retain much of larger teachers' performance. Treated as a system-level primitive rather than a single loss term, KD can transfer logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational knowledge; be combined with data synthesis, multi-teacher schedules, and architecture-aware alignments; and integrate with complementary compression techniques such as pruning and quantization. KD's empirical breadth across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, and its ability to transfer useful inductive biases, make it the recommended first-line method for many production compression pipelines. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality and compatibility, data availability and fidelity, and awareness of failure modes (teacher errors, distribution shift, rare-token loss, and robustness/fairness transfer). Practical deployment requires explicit design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which complementary steps (data strategies, precision reduction, pruning) to apply.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multi‑Strategy Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to compressing large models into smaller, efficient students. When treated as a toolbox of complementary methods—logit-level supervision, representation matching, layer alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data synthesis, and privacy-aware mechanisms—KD enables compact models to approach the performance of larger teachers while meeting real-world constraints on latency, memory, and data access. At the same time, distillation outcomes depend on teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization choices; addressing these limits requires careful method selection and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models into smaller, more deployable student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels — output logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure — and are commonly combined with architecture-level compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and training strategies (online co-training, curriculum schedules, synthetic-data protocols). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while improving latency and memory usage, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and appropriate choice of transfer signal. Ongoing challenges include robust transfer under distribution shift, aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and operating in data-limited or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful and practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD should be treated not as a single loss term but as a system-level design primitive that is chosen and tuned to match teacher–student capacity, data availability, deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy), and architectural heterogeneity. When designed with appropriate distilled signals, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), projector or alignment modules, and complementary compression techniques, distillation reliably enables compact, efficient models for real-world NLP and deep-learning applications. However, careful attention to teacher quality, student capacity, optimization dynamics, and domain shift is required to avoid failure modes and degraded behavior.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for converting large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, and multimodal settings KD has been shown to recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost and memory footprint. The technique comprises multiple transfer targets (soft outputs/logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and schedules (offline teacher supervision, online co-training, multi-teacher ensembles). Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, and must attend to data availability, teacher-student capacity alignment, and distributional robustness. Open challenges include data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, reliable transfer under domain shift, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors in NLP, and mitigating transfer of biases or teacher errors.
