papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost while retaining performance. A broad family of approaches—from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free synthesis, and federated or privacy-aware protocols—enables deployment across vision, speech, and language tasks. Practical success depends on matching the distillation signal to student capacity, combining KD with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, pretraining), and addressing data, optimization, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models to reduce inference cost while attempting to preserve predictive performance. KD encompasses a range of mechanisms — soft-target (logit) matching, feature and intermediate-layer imitation, attention- or channel-based guidance, ensemble-to-single-model transfer, self-distillation, and data- or device-aware variants — and is applied across modalities including vision and language. Empirical work shows KD can yield substantial reductions in parameters and latency with modest accuracy loss, and in some settings can improve student generalization. Practical deployment couples KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires careful design choices around teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific objectives.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more expressive models to smaller, efficient models to enable practical deployment without excessive loss in performance. These methods include matching teacher soft outputs, feature-level alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and architecture-aware strategies for heterogeneous settings. Across domains—vision, speech, NLP, and recommender systems—distillation is used both to compress models for latency and memory constraints and to inject complementary knowledge (e.g., cross-task or cross-modal signals). Empirical work shows that careful design choices (e.g., mixing hard/soft targets, projector modules, or student-aware teacher training) and task-specific adaptations address common pitfalls such as information loss on rare tokens or domain shifts. Open directions include stronger theoretical understanding, robustness under imperfect teachers, and principled integration with quantization, federated settings, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones in deep learning and NLP. Treated as a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s performance when its objectives, targets, and training strategies are matched to deployment constraints and student capacity. Effective application requires combining KD variants with complementary compression techniques and careful evaluation of robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Cardenas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable family of methods for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD can preserve most of a teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints; it is applied across modalities (vision, language, speech, multimodal) and is routinely combined with complementary compression techniques. However, KD’s benefits depend strongly on choices about what is distilled (logits, features, attention, relational structure), teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free settings), and deployment constraints; addressing domain shift, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, and avoiding undesirable property transfer remain important open challenges. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central component of modern compression pipelines while recognizing its context-dependent limits and recommending pragmatic combinations with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a practical toolkit for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, success hinges on what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals), how teacher–student mismatches and data constraints are handled, and how distillation is combined with complementary strategies (pretraining, architecture choices, and data-centric methods). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve most teacher performance under many conditions, but open problems remain in data-free and privacy-preserving settings, robust transfer under heterogeneity, and automated trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a primary, practical strategy for compressing large deep models into small, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD is flexible: it supports soft-target transfer, intermediate representation matching, attention-guided feature matching, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with architecture-aware design, low-precision numerics, and data synthesis or augmentation, KD produces compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. However, effective deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to mitigate risks such as transferred biases, robustness loss, and teacher–student mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide effective ways to reduce the computational and memory costs of large deep models while retaining much of their performance. Approaches span soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-level matching, data-augmentation and data-free techniques, and multi-teacher or teacher-optimization strategies. Recent work emphasizes task-aware alignment between teacher and student representations, augmentation schemes that improve teacher-student consistency, and training teachers that are explicitly optimized to help downstream students, enabling more reliable deployment in low-resource and privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and inference cost across vision and language tasks. When treated as a flexible toolkit—combining soft-target transfer, representation-level supervision, multi-teacher schedules, data- or privacy-aware synthesis, and integration with pruning/quantization/search—KD supports practical deployment under latency, memory, and data constraints. However, realizing its full potential requires careful teacher–student co-design, attention to data availability (including data-free and zero-shot approaches), and task- or architecture-aware objectives to avoid optimization and distributional failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster ones while preserving performance, enabling deployment under resource, latency, privacy, and domain-specific constraints. Across modalities and tasks, KD can be combined with architectural search, feature-level objectives, teacher optimization, and data-free methods to meet diverse production requirements. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a primary instrument in model-compression toolkits for modern deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has diversified from matching soft logits to a family of techniques that include intermediate feature and attention imitation, projector- or layer-aware mapping, ensemble and curriculum strategies, and data-free or privacy-preserving variants. Practical pipelines typically combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic examples) to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints, while facing challenges from teacher–student mismatch, data availability, and robustness or bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the first-line strategy for compressing large deep models into deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD offers a flexible set of mechanisms — from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-representation and attention-level imitation — that consistently reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when teacher–student alignment, data availability, and task-specific objectives are explicitly addressed. KD is not a universal cure: limits arise from optimization mismatches, teacher quality, data scarcity, and robustness concerns, so careful design and evaluation are required.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, often ensemble or higher-capacity teacher models to smaller student models to improve accuracy, robustness, interpretability, or resource efficiency. Over the past decade KD has been adapted beyond the original soft-label logits transfer: methods now target intermediate features, attention maps, channel-wise signals, and training curricula; they address deployment constraints such as low-precision arithmetic, absence of original data, heterogeneous device models, and federated settings. In NLP, distillation has been applied to compress pretrained language models, to enable multi-task or lifelong learning, and to improve robustness in tasks such as question answering and machine translation. Practical recipes combine architectural adjustments, selective or staged distillation, and application-specific modifications to retain teacher strengths while avoiding transferred errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation can be combined with architectural replacement, layer mapping, and task-adaptive search to produce compact models that meet latency and capacity constraints. However, the benefits of distillation depend strongly on teacher quality, data complexity, and which examples or representations are used for transfer; naive application can propagate teacher errors or harm low-frequency predictions. Careful design—using task-aware compression, selective or mixed supervision, and targeted remedies for dataset artifacts—enables distillation to deliver efficient, robust models for real-world NLP and vision systems.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Aware Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of the teachers' predictive power. When combined with representation matching, architecture-aware alignment, pre-training of compact models, and appropriate data strategies, KD reliably improves inference efficiency while preserving accuracy in many vision and language tasks. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: it requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or heterogeneous data and fairness constraints. Pragmatic deployment therefore treats KD as a first‑line method that must be adapted to task, data, and resource constraints rather than a one‑size‑fits‑all recipe.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models so as to reduce inference cost while preserving predictive performance. KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or zero-shot methods for cases where original training data are unavailable. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression building blocks (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when design choices account for teacher–student capacity, data availability, and task-specific objectives. Remaining practical challenges include robust transfer under distribution shift, preserving fine-grained behaviors (e.g., rare tokens or safety-critical outputs), and principled methods for data-free or privacy-sensitive distillation.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary, System-Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach that should be treated as the first-line, system-level strategy for compressing large models into deployable students. When KD is applied as a design primitive — selecting which signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods and data strategies — it yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, reliable deployment requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying deep models under resource constraints. Methods extend beyond simple logit matching to include intermediate-layer supervision, feature mimicking, projector-based transforms, teacher-student co-training, and data- or domain-aware schemes. Distillation has been applied across modalities (vision, language, multimodal, graphs) and in settings with limited or no access to original training data. Practical advances address transfer across architectures, task-adaptive compression, and efficient architecture search, while open problems remain around distribution shift, heterogeneity of data or detectors, and preserving rare or low-frequency information.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Dependent Path to Compact NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. When combined with complementary strategies—appropriate pretraining, architecture-aware compression, data management, or teacher-free alternatives—KD can produce compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. However, KD is not a universal remedy: success depends on what is distilled, how student and teacher are matched, the availability and provenance of data, and the need to manage transferred biases, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster ones while preserving much of their performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques—logit matching, feature- and attention-level transfer, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-student schemes, and hybrid pipelines combined with pruning or architecture modification—that make it adaptable to diverse deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). When applied with attention to the form of transferred knowledge, teacher quality, and data strategies, KD yields compact models suitable for production NLP and cross-modal systems; however, careful design is required to avoid pitfalls such as degraded calibration, transferred biases, or student–teacher mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a toolbox rather than a single loss term, KD delivers meaningful efficiency gains across modalities when the distillation targets, student design, and data strategy are chosen for the deployment constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis methods, and robustness to distribution shift. Practical success therefore requires combining KD with complementary compression techniques, carefully selecting what to transfer, and evaluating students under realistic deployment conditions.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision, speech, and NLP tasks, KD variants — including soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble guidance, self-distillation, and progressive module replacement — have been shown to reduce inference cost and memory while retaining much of the teacher's utility. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary techniques (data augmentation, low-precision numerics, teacher adaptation, and data-filtering) and must manage failure modes stemming from teacher–student capacity mismatch, data availability, and domain shift. The field continues to refine what knowledge to transfer, how to perform transfer efficiently, and how to preserve robustness and privacy in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical tool for compressing large models into efficient students while acknowledging that its effectiveness depends critically on task, data, teacher–student alignment, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, pretraining, and data strategies), KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs, but reliable production use requires deliberate signal selection, capacity-aware alignment, and privacy- or data-sensitive adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques train compact student models to emulate larger teachers, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across vision, speech, and language tasks. The body of work spans logits- or soft-target matching, feature- and layer-wise representation transfer, architecture-aware transformations, data-free and privacy-preserving methods, and multi-teacher or progressive schemes. Empirical and theoretical studies together show KD often improves student generalization and enables substantial efficiency gains, but outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and distribution, and optimization choices. Practical pipelines combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search while addressing failure modes such as teacher errors, low-frequency token degradation, and domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Insufficient Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach for converting large neural teachers into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when applied thoughtfully, but it is not a standalone solution: real-world compression requires attention to what is transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data provenance and availability, robustness and safety concerns, and the coordinated use of complementary compression methods such as architecture search, pruning, and curriculum or data strategies. Treating KD as a system-level primitive and combining it with targeted interventions produces the most reliable, efficient, and robust compressed models for production NLP and deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has grown from matching softened output distributions to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data-free/zero-shot synthesis, and architecture-aware co-design. Empirical work demonstrates KD's ability to reduce parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks; its practical success depends on careful choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to manage data and augmentation. Remaining challenges include robust distillation under domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior in language models, privacy-sensitive settings, and principled combination of KD with other compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision, speech, and NLP tasks, KD variants — including soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble guidance, self-distillation, and progressive module replacement — have been shown to reduce inference cost and memory while retaining much of the teacher's utility. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary techniques (data augmentation, low-precision numerics, teacher adaptation, and data-filtering) and must manage failure modes stemming from teacher–student capacity mismatch, data availability, and domain shift. The field continues to refine what knowledge to transfer, how to perform transfer efficiently, and how to preserve robustness and privacy in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Across vision and language tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-label transfers to a rich family of techniques including internal representation matching, attention- and channel-guided supervision, multi-teacher and ensemble signals, data-free and augmentation-driven methods, and architecture-aware transformations. Practical deployments combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search and must balance transfer of useful teacher information against risks such as propagating teacher errors or overfitting under limited data. The field continues to refine what teacher knowledge to transfer, how to synthesize or augment training data when it is unavailable, and how to align heterogeneous teacher–student architectures for robust, resource-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context‑Dependent Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic family of techniques for turning large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable ones. When treated as a system‑level design choice rather than a single loss term, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and inference cost while often preserving much of a teacher's predictive power. Realizing these benefits in practice requires choosing what knowledge to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities, and combining KD with complementary practices such as compact pre‑training, data augmentation, or privacy‑aware data synthesis. KD is powerful but not universal: its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher quality, and deployment constraints, so practitioners must evaluate and adapt distillation strategies to their task and context.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a broadly useful, pragmatic approach for shrinking large models into deployable students across vision, speech, and language tasks. Treated as a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants. When combined with complementary structural compression (pruning, quantization) and student-aware curricula, KD frequently achieves large reductions in memory and latency while retaining most of teacher performance. However, realizing these gains in production requires careful attention to what is transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit evaluation of robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone of Model Compression: Capabilities, Variants, and Contextual Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. KD supports a broad set of objectives—matching logits, aligning internal representations, using online or multi-teacher schemes, and operating with or without original training data—so it serves as the backbone of many modern compression pipelines. However, its success is context-dependent: choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data availability, and deployment constraints determine outcomes, and KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques and principled training workflows.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical First-Line Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (softened logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, ensemble consensus), and by combining distillation with data strategies and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely produces compact models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: careful selection of distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, data augmentation or synthesis, and evaluation under realistic distribution shifts are necessary to avoid failure modes. Treated as a system-level pipeline rather than a single loss, KD is the recommended first-line strategy for practical model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a General-Purpose Compression Strategy for Deep Models: Evidence, Mechanisms, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a specialized technique for transferring softened output distributions into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models across domains (vision, language, multimodal, and generative models). Empirical results across tasks show that KD can preserve or even improve accuracy while substantially reducing model size and latency, and it can be combined with complementary strategies (pre-training, low-precision arithmetic, data synthesis, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints and privacy requirements. However, effective distillation requires attention to what is transferred (logits, internal representations, attention maps), how teachers and students are aligned (layer mapping, input alignment), and whether real data are available (data-free or adversarially guided generation). This paper synthesizes evidence from recent work to argue that KD, when applied with these considerations, is a reliable foundation for practical model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach for producing compact, deployable deep models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and ensemble guidance, online/co-distillation variants, and data- or device-aware adaptations. In practice KD is combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search and task-aware design to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical evidence shows KD can yield large reductions in model size and inference cost with modest loss in accuracy, but persistent challenges remain in handling distribution shift, scarce or private data, transferring rare-token behavior in NLP, and avoiding unintended transfer of biases. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative application patterns, practical trade-offs, and recommended design choices for applying KD effectively in vision and language systems.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically supported path to compress large models into compact, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When treated as a central design pattern rather than a single loss term, KD enables multiple transfer targets (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), multi-teacher and online schedules, and integration with architecture-aware design and other compression methods. Practical success requires explicit attention to teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including pre-training of compact architectures and data augmentation or synthesis), and theoretical understanding of when soft versus hard supervision helps. Framed this way, KD is the most practical, multi-strategy mechanism for real-world compression, provided practitioners pair it with complementary techniques and careful evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Foundation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers substantial reductions in parameter count, latency, and memory while retaining much of teacher performance when applied with attention to what knowledge is transferred, teacher–student alignment, and data constraints. Its power lies in a broad toolkit—logit matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble guidance, data-free or adversarial synthesis, and integration with pruning, quantization, or architecture search—but it is not a universal remedy: careful method selection, mitigation of distribution shift and fairness/privacy risks, and complementary compression steps are required to realize robust, production-ready students.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or complex models into smaller, faster, or more constrained students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher. Over the past decade this has produced a diverse set of recipes — from logits/soft-label supervision to feature and layer-wise matching, progressive module replacement, data-free or privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/online variants — that together address deployment, privacy, robustness, and resource heterogeneity. Empirical work demonstrates that distilled students can approach teacher performance in NLP and vision tasks while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, or operation on weak devices; theoretical and empirical analyses illuminate when soft labels help, when hard labels or sample selection are needed, and how augmentation or task-aware selection of teacher knowledge improves transfer. Remaining challenges include principled understanding of which teacher signals are most useful for a given target task and resource constraint, robust and private distillation without original data, and scalable distillation in large distributed training regimes.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have diversified from the original logits-based teacher→student paradigm into a broad set of methods that operate on features, modules, data, and training procedures. Contemporary work shows multiple complementary mechanisms for transferring knowledge—soft targets, feature- and attention-level mimicry, adversarial alignment, module replacement, and data- or communication-constrained distillation—each suited to different deployment constraints (privacy, compute, bandwidth) and model families (transformers, CNNs, GANs, GNNs). Advances emphasize (1) understanding why KD helps (stability, richer concept learning), (2) designing where to transfer knowledge (penultimate features, attention maps, projectors), and (3) tailoring the distillation process to practical settings (online multi-model training, federated environments, data-free scenarios, and teacher models optimized for students). Empirical results across vision, speech, language, generation, and retrieval indicate KD can yield compact models that retain most teacher performance when the distillation objective, the representation level, and the training dynamics are appropriately matched to the target constraints.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Effective Knowledge Distillation for Deployable Deep Models: Evidence, Techniques, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool to compress large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and broader deep learning applications, KD has enabled domain adaptation, model-size reduction, cross-lingual transfer, and deployment under resource constraints. Success depends on (1) aligning teacher and student inputs and intermediate representations, (2) choosing appropriate supervision signals (soft labels, intermediate-feature losses, attention-based guidance), (3) handling the absence of original training data when necessary, and (4) adapting compression to task and domain requirements. This review synthesizes empirical and methodological findings from recent studies to recommend principled KD choices for practitioners aiming to deploy compact, robust models in real-world NLP and related tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. When integrated with task-aware student design, data or augmentation strategies, and complementary compression techniques, KD reliably reduces memory, compute, and latency while preserving—or sometimes improving—accuracy and specific properties (e.g., robustness or multimodal capabilities). This paper argues that KD should be treated as the primary, adaptable instrument in model-compression toolkits for practical deep-learning and NLP systems, and outlines concrete mechanisms and caveats for its application.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Current Understandings of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used model compression paradigm in which a smaller student model is trained to capture the behavior of a larger teacher model. It has been applied across domains (vision, NLP, recommender systems, medical imaging) to reduce model size and latency while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Work in the field explores what is transferred (soft outputs, internal representations, feature relations), how to improve transfer (adversarial samples, contrastive objectives, structural transformations), and how to address practical constraints (absence of original data, domain shift, privacy, fairness and robustness). Empirical results show KD often yields substantial memory and runtime benefits with modest accuracy loss and can be combined with pruning, quantization and architecture search. Yet KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, imperfect teacher signals, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity can limit how closely a student matches a teacher; research continues into theoretical explanations and robust, data-efficient methods.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. The field comprises a family of methods that transfer different forms of information—from soft logits to internal representations, attention maps, and relational structure—and integrates naturally with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Success depends on choosing what to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities and architectures, managing data availability (including data-free or federated setups), and designing appropriate optimization curricula. While KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, important limitations remain around teacher–student mismatch, domain shift, rare-token preservation in NLP, and robustness under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Responsible Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach that compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble consensus. KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance across modalities (NLP, speech, vision) and tasks. Its practical success depends on the choice of distilled signals, data strategies, and teacher-student design; when combined with augmentation, ensemble guidance, or privacy-aware mechanisms, KD supports real-world deployment while requiring safeguards against bias, privacy leakage, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Backbone with Bounded Limits for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, practical strategy for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels and, when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression techniques, yields efficient models suitable for latency- and memory-constrained deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and objective design, and practitioners must address robustness, fairness, and task-specific constraints to realize reliable compressed models.
