papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for reducing model size and inference cost while preserving or even improving generalization. The field combines a variety of approaches — from logit-level transfer to feature- and attention-level imitation, from data-free synthesis to multi-teacher ensembles and task-adaptive architecture search — and is applied across domains including NLP, vision, speech and healthcare. Contemporary work integrates distillation with pruning, neural architecture search, federated and privacy-preserving training, and meta-learning for better teacher-student alignment. Empirical results show substantial compression and speedups with modest accuracy loss when distillation is combined with architecture-aware optimization and data- or task-aware strategies. Ongoing challenges include handling imperfect teachers, distribution shift of synthetic data, privacy constraints, and transferring inductive biases across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic into a central, practical toolkit for compressing large models and transferring behavior from high-capacity teachers into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and generative modeling, practitioners combine soft-label supervision, intermediate-representation matching, data- and privacy-aware strategies, and architecture-aware choices to trade accuracy for latency, memory, and power. KD is effective when paired with complementary techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, synthetic-data generation, curriculum schedules), but its success depends critically on what form of knowledge is distilled, how data or augmentations are used, and how teacher–student capacity and domain mismatches are managed. Remaining challenges include robust data-free distillation, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, mitigating bias transfer, and firm theoretical characterizations that predict when and how distillation will work in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Responsible Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring useful predictive and representational knowledge from teacher models to students. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, multi-teacher weighting, data-free synthesis, pruning, and quantization) and guided by student-aware design and fairness/robustness constraints, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of a teacher's accuracy. Practical deployment of KD requires attention to data availability, teacher quality, and domain-specific constraints to avoid propagating undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large neural networks for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Beyond simple model-size reduction, KD enables transfer of inductive biases, domain adaptation, privacy-preserving distributed training, data-free and zero-shot compression, and the transfer of adversarial robustness. Combining logit-based distillation with feature-level mimicking and carefully chosen regularization yields high-quality small models that remain competitive on downstream tasks in NLP and broader deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applicable strategy for compressing large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models. When designed with attention to what is transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals), how teacher and student are aligned, and the data available for training, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of the original performance. KD also integrates naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adapts to specialized settings such as multi-teacher ensembles, heterogeneous-device deployments, generative-model compression, low-precision inference, and privacy-sensitive or data-limited environments. However, KD is not uniformly automatic: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, student capacity, distributional match, and design of distillation objectives and curricula.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the System-Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as a central, system-level approach to model compression and adaptation. By transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure from larger teachers to smaller students, KD enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints while preserving much of teacher performance. Real-world success depends on co-designing teacher and student, selecting what signals to transfer, combining distillation with complementary compression techniques, and using data strategies (including data-free or few-shot protocols) to handle privacy- or data-limited settings. When applied thoughtfully, KD serves as a unifying, practical toolkit for creating efficient, deployable models across modalities; however, careful mitigation of teacher-induced biases, distribution shift, and robustness issues is required.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful and practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD should be treated not as a single loss term but as a system-level design primitive that is chosen and tuned to match teacher–student capacity, data availability, deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy), and architectural heterogeneity. When designed with appropriate distilled signals, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), projector or alignment modules, and complementary compression techniques, distillation reliably enables compact, efficient models for real-world NLP and deep-learning applications. However, careful attention to teacher quality, student capacity, optimization dynamics, and domain shift is required to avoid failure modes and degraded behavior.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of model-compression techniques that trains smaller student models to reproduce useful behavior from larger teacher models. Across vision and language tasks, KD methods extend beyond matching soft teacher outputs to include alignment of internal representations, attention or relational signals, adversarially-informed objectives, online or multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware strategies. Effective application balances what is transferred, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis, and robustness or fairness constraints, and it is typically combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search for deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compact, High-Quality Models in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models for deployment. Across NLP and other modalities, distillation enables lightweight architectures to retain much of a teacher's performance while supporting additional compression techniques (pruning, quantization) and privacy-respecting or data-free workflows. However, distillation outcomes depend strongly on teacher–student compatibility, the form of distilled knowledge (logits, features, attention), access to data, and optimization choices. Best results arise when distillation is integrated with appropriate pre-training, architectural adapters (projectors or attention alignment), and, when necessary, data synthesis or domain adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models or ensembles into smaller, deployable student models. Methods range from matching teacher outputs (soft logits) to supervising intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and may be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance across modalities, but practical success depends on teacher–student alignment, data availability, robustness to domain shift, and choices about what form of knowledge to distill.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD techniques span soft-label transfer, intermediate representation matching, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and ensemble guidance, and adaptations for constrained or distributed settings. When combined with careful pretraining, representation-aware losses, selective sample strategies, and attention to privacy or robustness requirements, KD enables practical deployment of high-quality models on resource-limited devices and in federated environments.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, often over-parameterized teacher models into smaller, more efficient students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD strategies vary in what is transferred (soft targets, intermediate representations, relations), how it is transferred (logit matching, feature-mimicking, projector layers, contrastive objectives, adversarial losses), and in deployment settings (data-available, data-free, federated or distributed, and online). Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, distilled students frequently recover much of teacher performance while enabling practical gains in speed and memory; however, method choice, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and distributional shifts materially affect outcomes, and open problems remain in preserving rare-token behavior, transferring robustness and fairness, and compressing across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) unifies many successful strategies for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster ones that retain most of their performance. KD methods are adaptable across settings—from single-task NLP compression to large-scale distributed training and federated learning—and recent advances address core challenges such as teacher-student alignment, multi-teacher fusion, data scarcity, and domain shift. By combining architectural mapping, task-aware selection of distilled signals, dynamic teacher weighting, and online or data-free schemes, KD enables deployment of strong models in latency-, compute-, and privacy-constrained settings while exposing clear directions for further research.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. The field comprises a family of methods that transfer different forms of information—from soft logits to internal representations, attention maps, and relational structure—and integrates naturally with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Success depends on choosing what to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacities and architectures, managing data availability (including data-free or federated setups), and designing appropriate optimization curricula. While KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, important limitations remain around teacher–student mismatch, domain shift, rare-token preservation in NLP, and robustness under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Principled Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' predictive power. KD is most effective when it goes beyond naïve soft-label copying: matching internal representations, aligning inputs and tokenization, choosing appropriate data or synthesis strategies, and adapting teacher updates or curricula all materially affect transfer quality. KD should be used as part of a broader compression pipeline (architecture design, quantization, pruning, or data strategies) and with explicit checks for rare-token behavior, fairness, and robustness. When applied with these considerations, KD reliably produces compact models suitable for production constraints in vision, language, and other modalities.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: The Pragmatic Power and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured into a practical toolkit for shrinking models, transferring behavior across architectures and modalities, and enabling deployment under compute, memory, or privacy constraints. Beyond straightforward teacher-to-student compression, distillation techniques combine with data augmentation, synthetic-data generation, and regularization to address limited data, cross-domain gaps, and interpretability needs. However, outcomes depend on choices about teacher quality, training data availability, and objective design; careful method selection is required to realize reliable, production-ready gains.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of objectives and training regimes—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment, attention/relational signals, data- or privacy-aware synthesis, and teacher–student co-design—that together enable substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, available data, teacher/student compatibility, and complementary compression techniques; open challenges include robust transfer under domain shift, distillation without original data, and principled handling of heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) transfer into a broad toolkit that also includes intermediate representation matching, attention- and layer-aware objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and combinations with structural compression. Practical deployments of KD require careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, and how to handle limited or no access to original training data. While KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss in many settings, open problems remain in robustness under distribution shift, privacy- and data-constrained regimes, and principled selection of distilled signals for downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a General-Purpose Compression Strategy for Deep Models: Evidence, Mechanisms, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a specialized technique for transferring softened output distributions into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models across domains (vision, language, multimodal, and generative models). Empirical results across tasks show that KD can preserve or even improve accuracy while substantially reducing model size and latency, and it can be combined with complementary strategies (pre-training, low-precision arithmetic, data synthesis, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints and privacy requirements. However, effective distillation requires attention to what is transferred (logits, internal representations, attention maps), how teachers and students are aligned (layer mapping, input alignment), and whether real data are available (data-free or adversarially guided generation). This paper synthesizes evidence from recent work to argue that KD, when applied with these considerations, is a reliable foundation for practical model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a family of techniques that transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and compute while preserving task performance. KD methods range from transferring softened teacher outputs to matching intermediate representations or relational structure, and they are applied across modalities including language, vision, speech, and multimodal architectures. Practical deployments combine KD with architecture-aware transformations, low-precision numerics, data synthesis, and multi-stage training to address constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous devices, and privacy. While KD often yields strong empirical gains, success depends on choices about what to transfer, data availability and provenance, student architecture design, and optimization strategy; core open problems include handling teacher errors, preserving rare or fine-grained behavior, and reliably distilling across domain or architecture gaps.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Across vision and language tasks, KD has evolved from simple soft-label transfers to a rich family of techniques including internal representation matching, attention- and channel-guided supervision, multi-teacher and ensemble signals, data-free and augmentation-driven methods, and architecture-aware transformations. Practical deployments combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search and must balance transfer of useful teacher information against risks such as propagating teacher errors or overfitting under limited data. The field continues to refine what teacher knowledge to transfer, how to synthesize or augment training data when it is unavailable, and how to align heterogeneous teacher–student architectures for robust, resource-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for converting large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, and multimodal settings KD has been shown to recover a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost and memory footprint. The technique comprises multiple transfer targets (soft outputs/logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and schedules (offline teacher supervision, online co-training, multi-teacher ensembles). Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, and must attend to data availability, teacher-student capacity alignment, and distributional robustness. Open challenges include data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, reliable transfer under domain shift, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors in NLP, and mitigating transfer of biases or teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and complementary model-compression techniques transfer behaviors of large models into smaller, more efficient models by supervising students with information derived from teachers (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention, or synthetic labels). Empirical results across vision, speech, and language show that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve much of a teacher’s performance while reducing size and latency. Effective practice combines choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data strategies (including augmentation or synthesis), and complementary structural compression. Remaining challenges include handling imperfect teachers, limited or private data, robustness and out-of-distribution behavior, and principled automation of trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically proven approach for compressing large models into smaller, efficient students while preserving much of task performance. KD methods—ranging from soft-label matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online variants, and data-free techniques—enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation has well-documented failure modes (e.g., propagation of teacher errors, optimization mismatch) that require careful teacher/student design, data strategies, and complementary methods to get reliable results in practice.

papers_seen.author: Cardenas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable family of methods for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD can preserve most of a teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints; it is applied across modalities (vision, language, speech, multimodal) and is routinely combined with complementary compression techniques. However, KD’s benefits depend strongly on choices about what is distilled (logits, features, attention, relational structure), teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free settings), and deployment constraints; addressing domain shift, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, and avoiding undesirable property transfer remain important open challenges. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central component of modern compression pipelines while recognizing its context-dependent limits and recommending pragmatic combinations with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Weiss
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Multifaceted, and Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals) and by integrating with data strategies and complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, data provenance and coverage, and evaluation of rare-token, robustness, and fairness behaviors. Practitioners should therefore treat KD as a core design paradigm that is adapted to task, architecture, and deployment constraints and paired with complementary methods and targeted evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Foundation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical, flexible path to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Through a variety of transfer targets and training schedules, KD enables major reductions in parameter count, memory use, and latency while often preserving most of a teacher’s task performance. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, student pre-training and capacity, availability or synthesis of data, and complementary compression steps. KD is best treated as a toolkit to be combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and evaluation under realistic deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The method encompasses supervising students with softened teacher outputs as well as transferring intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful choices about data, teacher–student alignment, and optimization protocols, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Important open challenges include handling data-poor or data-free settings, mitigating transfer of undesirable behaviors (bias, privacy leakage), and reliably transferring rare or fine-grained knowledge across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse toolkit for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity models to smaller or otherwise constrained models. Approaches span from matching outputs to mimicking intermediate representations, from layer-aware mapping strategies to task-adaptive architecture search, and include protocols for heterogeneous, data-constrained, or privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical results across vision and language tasks demonstrate strong gains in efficiency with modest drops (or even improvements) in performance, while persistent challenges remain in handling data heterogeneity, choosing appropriate sources of knowledge, and designing robust data-free or federated distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a set of techniques to transfer knowledge from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students). Approaches vary from soft-label supervision and internal representation matching to data-free synthesis, task-adaptive architecture search, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols. Empirical results across vision and language tasks show distilled students can approach teacher performance while enabling deployment under computational, storage, privacy, or bandwidth constraints; open challenges include robustness, heterogeneity of data and models, and few-shot or label-scarce regimes.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Multifaceted, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central practical technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their predictive power. When combined with complementary strategies—task-aware objectives, intermediate representation matching, online or distributed schemes, and teacher-student co-design—KD supports deployment on resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive environments. Nonetheless, its effectiveness depends strongly on teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability (including few-shot or data-free regimes), and the choice of distilled signals; recognizing these dependencies leads to principled best practices that balance fidelity, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large neural networks for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Beyond simple model-size reduction, KD enables transfer of inductive biases, domain adaptation, privacy-preserving distributed training, data-free and zero-shot compression, and the transfer of adversarial robustness. Combining logit-based distillation with feature-level mimicking and carefully chosen regularization yields high-quality small models that remain competitive on downstream tasks in NLP and broader deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from one or more teachers. Across vision and language applications, KD has been adapted to handle teacher-free scenarios, multi-teacher setups, intermediate representation alignment, data- and domain-shift, and task-specific constraints such as ranking or retrieval. Empirical work shows that distillation can preserve much of teacher performance while dramatically reducing model size and latency, but practical success depends on what is transferred (soft outputs, internal features, or relational/contrastive knowledge), the quality and heterogeneity of teacher data, and training design choices such as data augmentation and curriculum. The literature also highlights cases where naive distillation propagates teacher errors (e.g., low-frequency lexical mistakes) and where alternative strategies (label smoothing view, internal representation matching, dynamic teacher weighting, or curriculum selection of examples) yield measurable improvements. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, common pitfalls, and promising methods for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the first-line strategy for compressing large deep models into deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD offers a flexible set of mechanisms — from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-representation and attention-level imitation — that consistently reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when teacher–student alignment, data availability, and task-specific objectives are explicitly addressed. KD is not a universal cure: limits arise from optimization mismatches, teacher quality, data scarcity, and robustness concerns, so careful design and evaluation are required.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. It delivers meaningful trade-offs between model size, latency, and retained performance when paired with appropriate distillation targets, student-aware design, and complementary compression techniques. However, KD’s success is conditional: it depends on teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability (including privacy constraints), the choice of distilled signals (soft targets versus intermediate features), and optimization practices. Best outcomes arise from task-aware distillation pipelines that combine soft-target transfer, representation-level supervision, and pragmatic strategies such as data synthesis, augmentation, or architecture-aware adjustments.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Compact, Robust Deep Models: Effectiveness, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD succeeds when its design (what to transfer, how, and with which data) is matched to deployment constraints: transferring logits, intermediate representations, or relational signals; using multi- or adaptive-teacher schedules; and combining distillation with model- and data-level compression. However, KD is not a panacea — optimization gaps, mismatched inputs or teachers, and inappropriate sample selection can degrade results — so robust application requires careful teacher-student co-design, selective supervision, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Findings, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring useful predictive behavior or internal structure from one or more teachers. A rich set of KD approaches exists — from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate representation imitation, attention and feature alignment, adversarial and projector-based techniques, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or federated variants — and these have been applied across NLP, vision, graph-structured data, multimodal models, and generative models. Empirical work shows KD often recovers much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher/student compatibility, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Important practical concerns include preserving rare-token behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher errors or biases, enabling privacy-preserving or data-free compression, and combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search).

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster ones while preserving performance, enabling deployment under resource, latency, privacy, and domain-specific constraints. Across modalities and tasks, KD can be combined with architectural search, feature-level objectives, teacher optimization, and data-free methods to meet diverse production requirements. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a primary instrument in model-compression toolkits for modern deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression are indispensable tools to deploy high-performing deep models under compute, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Across modalities and tasks, effective compression requires more than copying teacher logits: practitioners should match richer internal representations, align inputs and tokenization across teacher and student, design teacher updates that explicitly optimize transfer, and account for privacy and robustness needs. When applied thoughtfully, KD can produce compact models that retain much of the teacher’s utility and in some cases improve efficiency beyond the original models.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Dependent Path to Compact NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. When combined with complementary strategies—appropriate pretraining, architecture-aware compression, data management, or teacher-free alternatives—KD can produce compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. However, KD is not a universal remedy: success depends on what is distilled, how student and teacher are matched, the availability and provenance of data, and the need to manage transferred biases, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques that transfers information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD methods range from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or feature distributions, and can be combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) or data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing memory, compute, and latency, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the availability and provenance of data, and robustness to distributional shifts. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as one element of a broader compression toolkit and apply task- and deployment-aware design choices to balance fidelity and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single teacher→student soft-label transfer into a broad toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models across vision, language, and multimodal domains. Contemporary approaches extend logits matching to representation- and structure-aware objectives, multi- and continual-teaching schemes, task-aware layer selection, and combinations with pruning or architecture-level compression. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints but its success depends on design choices about what is transferred, how the student is supervised, data availability, and student capacity. Practical progress emphasizes representation matching beyond logits, careful layer- and channel-level alignment, and composing KD with other compression techniques; remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, data-free scenarios, and preserving fine-grained or safety-critical behavior.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more expressive models to smaller, efficient models to enable practical deployment without excessive loss in performance. These methods include matching teacher soft outputs, feature-level alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and architecture-aware strategies for heterogeneous settings. Across domains—vision, speech, NLP, and recommender systems—distillation is used both to compress models for latency and memory constraints and to inject complementary knowledge (e.g., cross-task or cross-modal signals). Empirical work shows that careful design choices (e.g., mixing hard/soft targets, projector modules, or student-aware teacher training) and task-specific adaptations address common pitfalls such as information loss on rare tokens or domain shifts. Open directions include stronger theoretical understanding, robustness under imperfect teachers, and principled integration with quantization, federated settings, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single loss term but as a system-level design primitive that is matched to data availability, deployment constraints, and student–teacher mismatch. When designers select what to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, or relational signals), how to expose the student to informative inputs (real, synthesized, or online peer predictions), and how to adapt protocols for distributed or privacy-sensitive settings, KD yields large practical gains in latency, memory, and deployability while controlling risks such as bias transfer or robustness loss. A deployment-aware KD practice leverages representation-aware objectives, data-free synthesis when training data are unavailable, adversarial or online schemes for richer alignment, and federated-distillation architectures for communication-efficient collaboration.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
