papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-strategy approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods include transferring softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and data-free or few-shot variants to handle limited or private data. Best results come from treating KD as one element of a broader compression pipeline that also incorporates architecture-aware choices, data strategies, and explicit attention to robustness and fairness. KD is therefore a central tool for efficient deployment, but it has clear limits and must be designed carefully to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or losing rare-token performance.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, Practical Outcomes, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, ensembling or progressive teacher schedules, and operating under data constraints (including data-free or synthetic-data strategies). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and student-aware design, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data provenance and availability, and training protocols; KD can propagate teacher errors (particularly for rare tokens/classes), degrade under distribution shift, and incur extra training overhead unless efficiency techniques are applied. Best practice treats KD as a flexible pipeline: choose appropriate distillation targets, reconcile architectural mismatches, use data strategies that match deployment constraints, and combine KD with other compression and robustness-aware methods.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a set of techniques to transfer knowledge from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students). Approaches vary from soft-label supervision and internal representation matching to data-free synthesis, task-adaptive architecture search, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols. Empirical results across vision and language tasks show distilled students can approach teacher performance while enabling deployment under computational, storage, privacy, or bandwidth constraints; open challenges include robustness, heterogeneity of data and models, and few-shot or label-scarce regimes.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a practical, versatile toolkit for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for deployment and adaptation in deep learning and NLP. When combined with representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance; at the same time, careful method choice is required to avoid pitfalls such as degraded rare-token behavior, transferred biases, and failures under limited or private data. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, but conditional, strategy for model compression and provides concrete recommendations for practitioners.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models or ensembles into smaller, efficient student models. KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, multi-teacher or online schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants; they are frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical results across vision, speech, language, generative, and 3D tasks show that distilled students can recover much of teacher performance when distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, and data strategies are chosen appropriately, but open problems remain around data-free scenarios, robustness to distribution shift, fairness, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD provides multiple channels of transferable information (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals) that, when combined with complementary techniques (architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, or data synthesis), produce compact models that retain much of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is context-dependent: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals and data, and attention to robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost while retaining performance. A broad family of approaches—from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free synthesis, and federated or privacy-aware protocols—enables deployment across vision, speech, and language tasks. Practical success depends on matching the distillation signal to student capacity, combining KD with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, pretraining), and addressing data, optimization, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical, flexible route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining a large fraction of teacher performance. KD spans multiple mechanisms — soft-target matching, intermediate-representation transfer, layer-wise or progressive replacement, privacy- and data-aware variants — and can be combined with structural compression such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is highly effective in many realistic settings but is not universally sufficient: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, what form of knowledge is transferred, data availability (including few-shot or privacy-constrained scenarios), and careful optimization and evaluation. Viewed as a central yet context-sensitive tool, KD should be a default component of compression pipelines, applied in concert with complementary methods and guarded by targeted diagnostics for robustness and rare-token or out-of-distribution behavior.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach for producing compact, deployable deep models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational and ensemble guidance, online/co-distillation variants, and data- or device-aware adaptations. In practice KD is combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search and task-aware design to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical evidence shows KD can yield large reductions in model size and inference cost with modest loss in accuracy, but persistent challenges remain in handling distribution shift, scarce or private data, transferring rare-token behavior in NLP, and avoiding unintended transfer of biases. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative application patterns, practical trade-offs, and recommended design choices for applying KD effectively in vision and language systems.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses information from larger or more informative models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relations. Across vision and language tasks, KD variants (soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, self-distillation, ensemble-to-single transfer, and projector- or channel-aware alignment) have been shown to recover much of the teacher’s performance while enabling lower-latency and lower-memory deployment. Practical success depends on choosing what to transfer, tailoring objectives to the student architecture and target task, and addressing data availability and teacher imperfections. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, representative methods, empirical patterns, and open challenges for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their predictive power. The approach spans simple logit matching to richer supervision such as intermediate-feature alignment, adversarial and online schemes, curriculum-driven supervision, and multi-teacher or self-distillation variants. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across vision, speech, and language tasks, but its success depends on what is transferred, the data used for distillation, and procedures that preserve robustness and domain generalization. Key challenges remain in handling heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, data scarcity or absence, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors in sequence models.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods for transferring behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment under resource constraints. Rather than a single algorithm, KD comprises multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational losses) and training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free) that should be chosen to match student capacity, data availability, and downstream requirements. Effective compression usually combines KD with complementary techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization) and careful alignment between teacher and student. Practical success thus depends on design choices and trade-offs rather than a universal distillation recipe.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable tool for shrinking large deep models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. When combined with complementary practices — careful teacher selection or adaptation, pre-training of compact architectures, feature-level matching, and privacy- or data-aware workflows — KD yields most of the practical benefits of compression while exposing clear trade-offs and failure modes. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the backbone of model compression pipelines, but that realizing reliable production gains requires principled choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, retrieval, and generation tasks. Contemporary KD methods extend far beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, curriculum and online schemes, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and tight integrations with architecture-level compression such as pruning and quantization. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but success depends on matched teacher–student design, the choice of distilled signals, data availability or synthetic-data alternatives, and careful evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare-class behaviors. Open challenges remain in domain-shift robustness, privacy-sensitive distillation, automated student architecture design, and principled selection of which aspects of teacher knowledge to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing compact models that meet deployment constraints in compute, memory, latency, and privacy. When integrated with complementary techniques (layer mapping, data strategies, adversarial training, and architecture-aware design), KD enables substantial compression with modest performance loss across vision and language tasks. Realizing these gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data. This paper argues that KD should be a first-line strategy in compression pipelines while outlining practical caveats and design recommendations for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of methods for transferring knowledge from larger, more expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so that the students retain much of the teachers' performance while meeting resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD methods include matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations or attention, synthesizing surrogate training data when original data are unavailable, and deploying progressive or ensemble-based strategies. Practical pipelines commonly combine KD with architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or search) and training-time strategies (curricula, online distillation, or federated protocols) to balance efficiency and accuracy. Despite strong empirical success across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, open challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, operating under limited or private data, and designing principled objectives and curricula that preserve robustness and task-specific inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Limits, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones that are deployable in resource-constrained settings. A rich set of distillation strategies has been developed: matching teacher output distributions, transferring intermediate representations, adversarial or data-free synthesis of training examples, multi-teacher aggregation, and contrastive or projector-based representation alignment. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance in many tasks (including NLP and graph learning), but practical success depends strongly on optimization details, the availability and alignment of data, and careful design of the distillation objective. Privacy-preserving variants and methods tailored to domain-specific architectures (e.g., GNNs, transformers) extend KD’s applicability, while also introducing trade-offs between utility, robustness, and guarantees. This synthesis summarizes key methods, empirical findings, and known limitations to guide research and practice in KD for deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP — Powerful, Context‑Dependent, and Best Used in Integrated Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When done beyond naïve soft-label copying—e.g., via intermediate-representation matching, attention or layer alignment, and careful teacher–student design—KD routinely delivers large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. Its strongest role is as a first-line, representation-aware strategy that is combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality and alignment, student capacity, data availability, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors and distributional failures. Practical deployment therefore requires principled recipes, diagnostics for failure modes, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A spectrum of distillation signals—soft logits, intermediate features and attention, relational/contrastive objectives, multi-teacher ensembles, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis—enables compact models that often retain most of teacher performance. Empirical results across NLP, speech, graph learning, and vision show KD’s practical value, while theoretical and empirical analyses point to mechanisms (soft-target regularization, ensemble-induced ‘‘dark knowledge’’, and representation shaping) and to limits tied to student capacity, data alignment, optimization dynamics, and robustness under distribution shift. Practical deployment requires careful selection of what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design).

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A diverse set of KD mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, attention- and relation-based signals, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data synthesis—has been developed and combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance in many vision and language tasks, while remaining sensitive to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, domain shift, and robustness concerns. Practical pipelines therefore co-design student architectures, distillation targets, and data handling strategies to achieve the best trade-offs for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single logit-matching trick into a versatile, task- and deployment-aware toolkit that can produce compact models with strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. By transferring soft targets, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and by integrating with architecture search, data augmentation, and heterogeneous-teacher setups, KD enables practical compression across vision and language modalities. This paper argues KD should be a first-line technique for model compression in deep learning and NLP, describes the complementary methods that make it effective in production settings, and highlights common pitfalls and practical remedies for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When paired with complementary compression methods and task‑aware design choices, KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of a teacher model’s performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on what is transferred, teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data‑free scenarios), and explicit treatment of robustness, rare‑token behaviors, and privacy. I argue that KD should be treated as a core engineering strategy whose full value is realized only when adapted to context through careful signal selection, data strategies, and architecture co‑design.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied model compression technique that trains a compact student model to emulate a larger teacher (or ensemble) so that inference cost and storage are reduced while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD has been adapted across domains (vision, graphs, NLP, multimodal systems) and combined with other compression methods; it can transfer logits, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge, and it can be extended to multi-teacher, self-distillation, and privacy-aware settings. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often improves generalization but also reveals limits and failure modes that motivate augmented objectives, data strategies, and teacher-training methods to achieve more effective, fair, and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can approach the performance of larger ones while meeting deployment constraints. KD methods vary in the form of transferred knowledge, how alignment is performed, and whether additional strategies (pruning, quantization, data synthesis) are used; empirical results show broad effectiveness across modalities but reveal important limitations and open problems around data availability, robustness, and preserving fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and compression seek to retain performance of large deep models while reducing size and latency for deployment. Methods extend beyond matching soft teacher outputs to include transferring internal representations, attention maps, and relational or adversarial signals; they can be applied during pretraining, task fine-tuning, or domain adaptation, and may operate with or without access to original training data. Empirical results across retrieval, reading comprehension, pretrained language models, and other domains show consistent trade-offs where careful choice of distillation targets, training curricula, and data augmentation materially improves student generalization and robustness while substantially lowering compute and memory requirements.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Powerful but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity and inputs, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD routinely reduces model size and latency while preserving much task performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-specific phenomena (e.g., rare-token behavior), so careful protocol design and evaluation under realistic constraints are essential.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Effective and Responsible Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Risks, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable deployment of large, high-performing deep models in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from a cumbersome teacher to a compact student. KD delivers large gains in inference speed and memory while preserving much of the teacher's utility across NLP tasks (including question answering and sentence understanding) and other modalities. However, naive distillation can transfer undesirable properties such as bias, privacy leakage, or fragility to distribution shift and adversarial attacks. A combination of strategies—student-aware teacher design, multi-teacher curricula, selective sample distillation, data augmentation, adversarial and robust distillation, and privacy-aware ensembles—provides a pragmatic path to compress models while controlling fairness, robustness, and privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and selected internal information from teacher models. KD methods range from matching softened teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and are commonly combined with complementary engineering strategies (architecture design, pretraining of compact models, quantization, and data augmentation). Empirical evidence shows distilled students can approach teacher performance across vision and language tasks while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability and augmentation, and the relative strength and role of the teacher; these choices shape practical tradeoffs in robustness, fairness, and cross-distribution generalization.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under memory, latency, or privacy constraints. Across computer vision, speech, and natural language processing, KD has evolved from matching teacher logits to a broad set of practices that include intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-free or black-box distillation, and architecture-aware compression. These methods routinely yield substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but success depends on choices about the type of knowledge transferred, the student initialization and capacity, the availability and provenance of data, and evaluation for robustness and undesired behavior.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques seek to reduce the runtime, memory, and deployment costs of large deep models while retaining their predictive performance or improving other desiderata (e.g., interpretability, fairness). Across vision and language domains, methods range from classical teacher-to-student soft-target distillation to transferring intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, selective sample-driven distillation, and teacher-adaptive or teacher-free schemes. Empirical work shows that carefully chosen distillation targets, alignment of intermediate representations, and input-side practices (such as tailored data augmentation) can materially affect student performance. Remaining challenges include representation mismatches between teacher and student, identifying which training samples are beneficial for transfer, and adapting distillation to domain- or resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a practical toolkit for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, success hinges on what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals), how teacher–student mismatches and data constraints are handled, and how distillation is combined with complementary strategies (pretraining, architecture choices, and data-centric methods). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve most teacher performance under many conditions, but open problems remain in data-free and privacy-preserving settings, robust transfer under heterogeneity, and automated trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from teacher models. KD encompasses a family of techniques — matching teacher logits (soft targets), aligning intermediate features or attention maps, online or mutual distillation, self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware variants — that are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of teacher performance in vision and language tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality and specialization, student capacity and architecture, availability and alignment of data, and optimization choices; naive distillation can propagate teacher errors or fail under strong teacher–student mismatch. Practical pipelines therefore select distillation signals and schedules appropriate to task and deployment constraints, often pairing KD with complementary compression techniques to trade compute and size for modest predictive degradation.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers information beyond hard labels — including softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals — and is commonly combined with architectural or numerical compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when teacher–student design, data availability, and optimization dynamics are considered; however, its success is contingent on capacity alignment, data choices, and safeguards against transferring undesirable behaviors. Applications range from accelerated inference and edge deployment to domain adaptation, federated learning, and task-specific adaptations such as non-autoregressive translation and graph-to-MLP compression.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression methods transfer knowledge from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving performance. Approaches span soft-label (logit) matching, feature- or attention-level imitation, multi-teacher fusion, data-free distillation, and adaptations for domain shift and heterogeneous deployment. Empirical results show distilled students can approach or match teacher performance in many settings, but success depends on teacher quality, the form of transferred knowledge, training curricula, and application-specific design choices. Emerging theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and reveal practical tradeoffs such as bias–variance effects of soft labels and the roles of ensemble and self-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. It delivers meaningful trade-offs between model size, latency, and retained performance when paired with appropriate distillation targets, student-aware design, and complementary compression techniques. However, KD’s success is conditional: it depends on teacher-student capacity alignment, data availability (including privacy constraints), the choice of distilled signals (soft targets versus intermediate features), and optimization practices. Best outcomes arise from task-aware distillation pipelines that combine soft-target transfer, representation-level supervision, and pragmatic strategies such as data synthesis, augmentation, or architecture-aware adjustments.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD techniques span soft-label transfer, intermediate representation matching, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and ensemble guidance, and adaptations for constrained or distributed settings. When combined with careful pretraining, representation-aware losses, selective sample strategies, and attention to privacy or robustness requirements, KD enables practical deployment of high-quality models on resource-limited devices and in federated environments.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches and Insights in Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer useful information from larger, more expensive models (or ensembles) to smaller, deployable models. Research spans theoretical analyses of what is transferred, architectural and loss-design strategies to improve feature and output matching, specialized teacher–student training regimes (including multi-teacher and student-aware teacher training), online and federated distillation for large-scale or privacy-sensitive settings, and structural compression strategies that preserve accuracy while reducing memory and compute. Applications include image models, generative models, question-answering systems and multi-task natural language understanding, with methods tailored to domain constraints such as heterogeneous device capabilities and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) unifies many successful strategies for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster ones that retain most of their performance. KD methods are adaptable across settings—from single-task NLP compression to large-scale distributed training and federated learning—and recent advances address core challenges such as teacher-student alignment, multi-teacher fusion, data scarcity, and domain shift. By combining architectural mapping, task-aware selection of distilled signals, dynamic teacher weighting, and online or data-free schemes, KD enables deployment of strong models in latency-, compute-, and privacy-constrained settings while exposing clear directions for further research.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable framework for producing compact models by transferring behavior from larger teachers to smaller students. KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under resource constraints, and it extends beyond simple logit matching to include feature-level imitation, self-distillation, data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its efficacy depends on teacher quality and compatibility, the choice of distilled information, data availability, capacity mismatch, and fairness or robustness concerns. A considered KD pipeline—combining soft-targets, internal representation guidance, task-aware objectives, and suitable data strategies—yields robust, efficient students fitting real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD is both a compression mechanism and a training-time regularizer: when carefully designed it preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and inference cost. However, KD’s success depends on choices about what to transfer (outputs, intermediate features, or both), how to align teacher and student architectures, what data are used (real, augmented, or synthetic), and whether deployment constraints (privacy, heterogeneity, federated settings) limit access to teacher data or models. A principled KD practice adapts targets, aligns representations where useful, addresses teacher–student mismatches, and recognizes scenarios where KD alone is insufficient.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Principled Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical technique for compressing large neural models into deployable, efficient students while preserving much of teacher performance. Across supervised, self-supervised, multi-task, and low-precision settings, distillation can recover large-model accuracy in smaller footprints when combined with careful design choices that address capacity mismatch, task relevance, and the nature of the transferred knowledge. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on distillation schedule, selection of what to transfer (logits, features, or task-aware subsets), and occasionally on teacher improvement or specialization. Understanding these interactions is key to robust compression for production NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in deep learning and NLP. A broad family of KD techniques—ranging from softened-logit supervision to intermediate representation matching, attention- and feature-level imitation, many-to-many layer alignment, adversarial and data-free variants, and task- or device-aware architecture search—enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often retaining most of the teacher's performance. Effective application requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, whether and how to use original data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. Important open problems remain regarding theoretical understanding, robustness under distribution shift or imperfect teachers, and scalable private or data-free distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool: Compression, Regularization, and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a compression heuristic into a versatile training paradigm that enables model size reduction, improved generalization, domain adaptation, and task consolidation. Its practical success depends on both the sources of teacher supervision (final logits, intermediate representations, or multiple teachers) and how distillation is applied (sample selection, layer matching, or label design). While KD frequently yields compact, high-performing models, its benefits arise from a mixture of transferred dark knowledge and regularizing effects of soft targets; careful design choices are required to realize those benefits across settings such as language model compression, multi-task training, and privacy-constrained or heterogeneous environments.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Rationale, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical, broadly applicable pathway to compress large neural models into smaller students that retain much of teacher performance. As a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD supports a range of transfer signals (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention and relational signals), and it integrates naturally with complementary compression mechanisms (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment constraints (latency, privacy, heterogeneity). KD delivers strong empirical gains across modalities and tasks when matched to student capacity and data conditions, but it is not a universal fix: success requires careful teacher–student design, data and curriculum strategies, and safeguards for distribution shift and rare-token fidelity. The position taken here is that KD should be treated as a first‑line, default strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP—used proactively and in combination with other compression primitives—while acknowledging its failure modes and design requirements.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transform large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster, and more deployable models. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, methods include soft-target (logit) distillation, feature and representation matching, layer-mapping strategies for large pretrained models, data- and privacy-aware protocols, and training-time variants such as online or co-distillation. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often retain much of teacher performance while yielding substantial savings in memory, latency, and energy; however, outcomes depend on teacher–student compatibility, access to task data, which signals are transferred, and training protocol choices. Key open problems include robust cross-domain transfer, handling teacher errors and low-frequency phenomena, and reducing distillation cost when teachers are large or data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Strategy Path to Compressing Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep models while preserving much of their performance. Across modalities and deployment settings, KD enables smaller models to inherit predictive behavior, internal structure, and cross-model insights from larger teachers. Best results arise when distillation is combined with complementary strategies — internal representation matching, curriculum scheduling, multi-teacher selection, data augmentation, meta-learned teachers, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols — yielding compact, efficient, and robust student models suitable for edge, federated, and low-precision deployments.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal information from teacher models. A rich toolbox has emerged—ranging from softened-output matching to intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with structural compression—that makes it possible to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints across vision and language tasks. Practical deployment requires attention to teacher–student compatibility, choice of distilled signals, data availability, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare-token and domain-specific behavior, and principled handling of teacher–student mismatch in heterogeneous settings.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the first-line strategy for compressing large deep models into deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD offers a flexible set of mechanisms — from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-representation and attention-level imitation — that consistently reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when teacher–student alignment, data availability, and task-specific objectives are explicitly addressed. KD is not a universal cure: limits arise from optimization mismatches, teacher quality, data scarcity, and robustness concerns, so careful design and evaluation are required.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practices, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers predictive behavior and internal structure through a range of signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals) and supports variants such as multi-teacher, online, adversarial, and data-free distillation. Its effectiveness depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, what and how knowledge is transferred, data availability (or synthetic data strategies), and complementary compression mechanisms (architecture search, pruning, quantization). While KD has enabled many real-world deployments across modalities, its limits include sensitivity to distribution shift, optimization mismatches, fairness and privacy concerns, and challenges in aligning heterogeneous architectures. Best practice treats KD as a core first-line strategy combined with targeted methods tailored to task, data, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Best Practices and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Efficient Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a foundational technique for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the accuracy of larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and graph domains. When applied thoughtfully — combining representational objectives, teacher-student co-design, task-aware compression, and appropriate data strategies — KD enables deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining robustness and fairness. However, pitfalls arise from mismatches in inputs, teacher strength, data availability, and dataset biases; practical KD should therefore be integrated with complementary methods (e.g., architecture search, pruning, curriculum strategies, and data-generation) and with safeguards for ethical concerns.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When combined with representation-level objectives, architecture-aware techniques, and deployment-aware protocols, KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling real-world constraints such as latency, memory, and device heterogeneity to be met. Best practices include selecting appropriate distilled signals (beyond soft labels), pretraining or warming students, and aligning objectives with deployment constraints. Despite strong empirical success across modalities, open challenges remain in handling data heterogeneity, domain shift, privacy-sensitive settings, and the automated design of student architectures.
