papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD enables deploying compact models that retain much of teacher performance, supports cross-modal and task-specific transfers, and can be adapted to privacy- and data-constrained settings. While highly effective in practice, KD’s outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and objective design; realizing its full potential requires targeted methodological choices such as feature-level matching, multi-teacher fusion, adversarial data synthesis, and privacy-preserving mechanisms.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Complementary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers real efficiency gains when its targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals) and training protocols are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its best use is as the central element of a compression pipeline that explicitly addresses teacher–student alignment, data availability, robustness, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success requires careful design of distilled signals, data or synthetic-data strategies, and evaluation under realistic distributional and fairness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Targeted Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for producing compact, deployable models by transferring behavior from larger teacher models into smaller students. The field has evolved beyond matching softened output logits to include representation-level guidance, attention and relational targets, data-augmentation and synthesis strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work across vision and language shows that appropriately designed distillation pipelines can recover much of teacher performance while reducing compute, memory, and latency; however, success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and provenance, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as one component of a compression toolkit, integrating architecture choices, precision reductions, and data strategies to meet production constraints.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from large teacher models or ensembles to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving task performance. The field encompasses soft-label (logit) supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, structural and architectural transformations, data-free and privacy-aware variants, multi-teacher and online distillation, and meta-learned teacher strategies. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often improves student generalization and enables deployment under resource constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on what signals are transferred, data availability and provenance, optimization dynamics, and teacher–student capacity gaps. Practical deployment requires choosing student architectures, distillation signals, and training regimes aligned to the target task and constraints; key open problems include robust data-free distillation, principled teacher design, and theoretical characterization of when different knowledge sources help.

papers_seen.author: Espinoza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Outcomes, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and selected internal signals from teachers. Over the past decade KD has broadened from simple soft-label matching to a diverse set of techniques — intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data- or generator-based synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirically, distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and training dynamics. Open problems remain in robustness to domain shift, preserving rare-token fidelity in sequence tasks, privacy- and data-constrained distillation, and principled selection of distilled signals for downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and selected internal information from teacher models. KD methods range from matching softened teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and are commonly combined with complementary engineering strategies (architecture design, pretraining of compact models, quantization, and data augmentation). Empirical evidence shows distilled students can approach teacher performance across vision and language tasks while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability and augmentation, and the relative strength and role of the teacher; these choices shape practical tradeoffs in robustness, fairness, and cross-distribution generalization.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Practical Strengths, Limits, and a Pragmatic Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible set of methods for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Over a range of modalities and tasks, KD variants transfer richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive objectives), and they can be combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, or synthetic-data generation) to meet deployment constraints. KD reliably improves efficiency–accuracy trade-offs when teacher and student are properly aligned and when the distillation strategy matches data and system constraints; however, it is not a universal solution. Key limitations include sensitivity to teacher–student capacity mismatch, degraded transfer on low-frequency or domain-specific phenomena, and challenges when original training data are unavailable or under distribution shift. A pragmatic KD practice chooses appropriate distilled signals, co-designs student architectures, uses synthetic or adversarially generated data when needed, and evaluates robustness and fairness under realistic deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically supported approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. When thoughtfully applied — selecting appropriate distillation signals, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques and data strategies — distillation enables large reductions in compute and memory with modest performance loss. However, KD is not universally sufficient on its own: outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and provenance, and optimization choices. Practical pipelines therefore treat distillation as a core element of a broader compression strategy, integrating pretraining, representation-aware objectives, multi-teacher curricula, and privacy- or data-constrained methods to produce robust, efficient models for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller students that can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD variants transfer soft targets, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or synthetic data, and they are often combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. While KD routinely produces strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, its effectiveness depends on careful choices about the distilled signals, teacher–student compatibility, data provenance (including data-free settings), and training regimes to preserve robustness and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Theory, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach to compress large deep models and transfer knowledge to smaller, faster, or more interpretable models. Across vision and language applications, KD encompasses teacher-student paradigms that use teacher soft targets, intermediate representations, or auxiliary objectives; extensions include multi-teacher setups, data-free distillation, meta-learned teachers, and device-aware distillation for heterogeneous deployments. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude reductions in parameters and inference cost; theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and how dataset complexity, teacher quality, and student capacity interact to determine outcomes. Practical strategies combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware techniques to meet deployment constraints while retaining generalization.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and practically central approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal settings. KD operates via multiple types of transferred signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and training regimes (offline teacher-to-student, online peer distillation, ensemble-to-student). In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture search) and when design choices about student capacity, data, and objectives are aligned with deployment constraints. Despite strong empirical success, open challenges remain around preserving robustness, fairness and rare-token behaviors, operating under limited or private data, and principled selection of what and how to distill.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from pre-trained teachers. The approach spans soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, layer-mapping strategies, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free workflows. Empirical results show KD often recovers much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and optimization protocols. Ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, maintaining robustness and fairness under distribution shift, and operating when original training data is limited or unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has evolved from matching softened logits to a broad family of methods that include intermediate-feature alignment, attention- and relation-based transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, data-free or synthetic-data strategies, and architecture-aware compression. Practically, KD enables favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks but requires careful design around the form of knowledge transferred, teacher–student compatibility, data availability and augmentation, and evaluation for robustness and undesired behavior. Open problems remain in reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors in sequence tasks, and ensuring fairness and robustness in deployed compact models.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster ones while preserving performance, enabling deployment under resource, latency, privacy, and domain-specific constraints. Across modalities and tasks, KD can be combined with architectural search, feature-level objectives, teacher optimization, and data-free methods to meet diverse production requirements. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a primary instrument in model-compression toolkits for modern deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Ball
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Powerful, Multifaceted, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical and versatile approach for compressing deep models for deployment in constrained environments. KD methods transfer predictive behavior and internal information from larger teachers to smaller students using a range of targets and training regimes; when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression steps, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, latency, and compute while retaining much of teacher performance. However, the method’s effectiveness depends on careful selection of transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of undesirable teacher behavior, so KD should be applied as part of an integrated compression strategy rather than a single silver-bullet solution.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Powerful, Practical, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are essential tools for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. A wide family of methods — from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature transfer, projector-based alignment, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning or architecture search — let practitioners trade compute and memory for modest accuracy loss. However, KD’s effectiveness depends on optimization, data alignment, and the choice of distilled signals; it can replicate undesirable teacher behaviors and fails when teacher–student mismatch or data constraints are not addressed. Practical deployment therefore requires selecting KD variants that match application constraints and combining distillation with complementary compression and robustness techniques.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students that retain much of the teacher's performance. Across NLP, vision, and generative models, KD takes many forms (soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention alignment, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher schemes, and data-free synthesis) and is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving accuracy under many conditions, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and optimization protocols. Practical deployment requires careful design choices and remains an active area for research on robustness, rare-token preservation, privacy, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Power, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for converting large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary strategies—pre-training compact architectures, feature-level supervision, multi-teacher schedules, data synthesis or augmentation, and task-aware student design—KD yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, choice of distilled signals, and data availability; without such care, distillation can underperform or lose task-specific signals. I argue KD should be the first-line approach for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP pipelines, provided practitioners adopt principled, context-aware distillation recipes.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach to compress large neural models for deployment, while preserving performance and enabling new capabilities such as efficient federated learning, data-free compression, interpretability, and few-shot adaptation. Across architectures and tasks, KD variants—ranging from layer-to-layer alignment and progressive module replacement to meta-learned teachers and adversarial data synthesis—provide methods to trade computation, memory, and communication for small changes in accuracy. These methods make it possible to bring large pretrained models into production and edge settings, and to reconcile competing requirements such as privacy, heterogeneity, and interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques that transfer information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational or contrastive signals), how data are used or synthesized, and how training is scheduled (offline, online, self-distillation, adversarial compression). Empirical work shows KD can enable deployable models across vision, speech, and NLP, but success depends on aligning teacher-student inputs and representations, addressing optimization mismatches, and adapting objectives to task and data constraints. Open challenges include data-free distillation, cross-domain generalization, robustness, fairness, and principled choices of distillation targets for heterogeneous student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse toolkit for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity models to smaller or otherwise constrained models. Approaches span from matching outputs to mimicking intermediate representations, from layer-aware mapping strategies to task-adaptive architecture search, and include protocols for heterogeneous, data-constrained, or privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical results across vision and language tasks demonstrate strong gains in efficiency with modest drops (or even improvements) in performance, while persistent challenges remain in handling data heterogeneity, choosing appropriate sources of knowledge, and designing robust data-free or federated distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD provides multiple channels of transferable information (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals) that, when combined with complementary techniques (architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, or data synthesis), produce compact models that retain much of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is context-dependent: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals and data, and attention to robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to which signals are transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention), the teacher–student relationship, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD yields substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher behavior. However, KD is not universally sufficient: its success depends on capacity alignment, data and distributional match, and careful objective design. Practical adoption therefore requires selecting KD variants that fit task and system constraints and combining KD with complementary techniques (pretraining, data augmentation, multi-teacher signals, or architecture co-design) to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Benefits, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and natural language processing. KD methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students using a variety of signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and configurations (single- or multi-teacher, online/offline, data-driven or data-free). When combined with complementary compression techniques and appropriate data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models with substantially reduced inference cost while retaining a large fraction of teacher performance. However, its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, the type and availability of data used for transfer, optimization dynamics, and downstream robustness, and so KD is best applied as one element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural teachers into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, KD techniques include soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention- or relation-based alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher fusion, and data- or domain-aware variations. Empirical work shows that distilled students often recover most teacher performance and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design to meet deployment constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and training objectives. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behavior, transferring robustness and inductive biases, and handling heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive environments.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad toolkit—logit-level supervision, intermediate-feature matching, layer-mapping, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants—has been developed to meet deployment constraints in vision and natural language tasks. Empirical work shows that, when combined with architecture-aware choices and complementary compression techniques, KD frequently yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, though careful method selection is required to mitigate mismatches, data limitations, and task-specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Espinoza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Outcomes, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and selected internal signals from teachers. Over the past decade KD has broadened from simple soft-label matching to a diverse set of techniques — intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data- or generator-based synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirically, distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and training dynamics. Open problems remain in robustness to domain shift, preserving rare-token fidelity in sequence tasks, privacy- and data-constrained distillation, and principled selection of distilled signals for downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad, practical toolkit for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, generative, and multimodal domains. Research shows KD can preserve—and in some settings improve—task performance while enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency when combined with complementary strategies. Practical success depends on what is transferred (outputs, internal features, attention), how teacher and student are aligned architecturally and procedurally, and on data and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) effectively compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble consensus. KD has matured into a versatile toolkit that, when combined with careful teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and targeted objectives. Best practice therefore treats distillation as the central element of a compression pipeline, augmented by augmentation, curriculum design, privacy-aware aggregation, and architecture-aware substitution to mitigate known failure modes and preserve robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a single recipe for shrinking large models: it is a versatile family of techniques that can preserve performance while enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings, but it must be adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints. Effective KD requires attention to the teacher-student relationship (including training teachers that are "student-friendly"), to data availability (including data-free approaches), and to distributional mismatches (e.g., federated or heterogeneous-device scenarios). When such concerns are addressed—via task-adaptive compression, feature- or relation-aware transfer, multi-teacher or ensemble signals, or methods that expose raw data signals lost in naive distillation—KD can deliver near-teacher performance at far lower cost. However, KD has known failure modes (such as propagating teacher errors on low-frequency tokens or degrading under data heterogeneity) that demand targeted remedies. This paper argues that KD should be treated as an adaptable design pattern: choose techniques that match your downstream objective (accuracy, latency, privacy, heterogeneity) rather than applying a one-size-fits-all distillation loss.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used approach to compress large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring useful information from a trained teacher. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a family of techniques that include feature- and attention-level imitation, progressive module replacement, self-distillation, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. Empirical work across computer vision, ranking, speech, and natural language tasks shows distilled models can approach teacher performance when distillation is matched to student capacity, task demands, and data availability. Practical deployment requires combining KD with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and fairness/privacy safeguards while managing trade-offs between fidelity, robustness, and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger ‘‘teacher’’ models to smaller ‘‘student’’ models to reduce compute, memory, and latency while preserving predictive performance. KD encompasses soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature matching, relational or attention-level supervision, multi-teacher and ensemble compression, and data-centered strategies including augmentation and data-free synthesis. When combined with architecture-aware design, pretraining, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization), KD enables practical deployment across vision, language, graph, and edge settings. However, its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and quality, optimization dynamics, and practical concerns such as privacy, robustness, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and broadly applicable technique to compress large neural models into smaller, faster models while preserving much of their performance. Work across computer vision, speech, and natural language processing demonstrates that KD can enable deployment of resource-efficient models, improve generalization in constrained settings, and be combined with other compression methods (e.g., low-precision numerics). At the same time, the field has identified important limitations and nuanced behaviors — such as data simplification effects, teacher–student mismatches, and domain or task-specific failure modes — that guide how KD should be applied in practice. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, variants, empirical benefits, and practical considerations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Powerful but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach to compress large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Its effectiveness arises from the ability to transfer different forms of knowledge (soft labels, intermediate features, attention, ensembles) and to combine distillation with data augmentation, pretraining, and task-aware objectives. However, KD is not uniformly successful: outcomes depend on teacher-student capacity alignment, the choice of distillation targets, data availability and augmentation strategy, and deployment constraints such as privacy or device heterogeneity. Careful selection of distillation signals, task-aware layer matching, and augmentation or synthetic-data strategies improve robustness; conversely, mismatches in architecture, domain shift, or heterogeneous federated settings can sharply limit benefits.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Across vision, speech, reinforcement learning, and NLP, KD has been adapted into logit-level supervision, intermediate feature and layer-wise matching, data augmentation strategies, data-free setups, and training-time architectural replacement. Recent work has expanded KD to address practical constraints—privacy in federated settings, bias mitigation in language models, low-precision deployment, and multi-task transfer—while also proposing task-aware and capacity-aware methods to reduce redundant or harmful teacher signals. This synthesis summarizes the mechanisms, extensions, strengths, and limitations documented in contemporary studies and highlights promising directions for making distilled models both efficient and robust.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line, System‑Level Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models that retain much of larger teachers' performance. Treated as a system-level primitive rather than a single loss term, KD can transfer logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational knowledge; be combined with data synthesis, multi-teacher schedules, and architecture-aware alignments; and integrate with complementary compression techniques such as pruning and quantization. KD's empirical breadth across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, and its ability to transfer useful inductive biases, make it the recommended first-line method for many production compression pipelines. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality and compatibility, data availability and fidelity, and awareness of failure modes (teacher errors, distribution shift, rare-token loss, and robustness/fairness transfer). Practical deployment requires explicit design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which complementary steps (data strategies, precision reduction, pruning) to apply.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students. KD enables deploying compact models that retain much of teacher performance, supports cross-modal and task-specific transfers, and can be adapted to privacy- and data-constrained settings. While highly effective in practice, KD’s outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and objective design; realizing its full potential requires targeted methodological choices such as feature-level matching, multi-teacher fusion, adversarial data synthesis, and privacy-preserving mechanisms.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models so that deployments meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational structures; they can be applied in offline, online, or multi-teacher regimes and combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability (including data-free or federated settings), and careful selection of distillation targets and training curricula. Remaining challenges include handling heterogeneous architectures, distribution shift, preservation of rare-class or rare-token behavior, and avoiding transfer of undesirable teacher biases or errors.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Across vision, language, and multimodal settings, KD variants—ranging from logits or soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment, attention- or feature-level matching, many-to-many layer mapping, meta-learned teachers, data-free synthesis, and federated or device-aware schemes—enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher utility. Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity, choosing appropriate distillation targets and curricula, and combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Remaining gaps include optimization dynamics, data- and privacy-limited scenarios, theoretical explanations of when distillation helps, and robustness to distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches and Insights in Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer useful information from larger, more expensive models (or ensembles) to smaller, deployable models. Research spans theoretical analyses of what is transferred, architectural and loss-design strategies to improve feature and output matching, specialized teacher–student training regimes (including multi-teacher and student-aware teacher training), online and federated distillation for large-scale or privacy-sensitive settings, and structural compression strategies that preserve accuracy while reducing memory and compute. Applications include image models, generative models, question-answering systems and multi-task natural language understanding, with methods tailored to domain constraints such as heterogeneous device capabilities and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Recipe
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the first-line, practical strategy for compressing large models in deep learning and NLP because it provides a flexible set of mechanisms to transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from high-capacity teachers to smaller, efficient students. KD recovers much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory footprint, and it composes naturally with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data synthesis). However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on what is distilled, how teacher and student are aligned, data availability, and robustness under domain shift or privacy constraints. A productive deployment strategy treats KD as the core of a hybrid pipeline, applies task-aware signal selection and layer alignment, uses multi- or student-aware teachers when appropriate, and combines distillation with lightweight model design and compression primitives to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated approach for converting large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Treated as a toolkit rather than a single loss, KD supports multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free), and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). I argue KD should serve as the first-line strategy for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP pipelines, provided practitioners adopt principled, context-aware distillation recipes and pair KD with targeted validation for robustness and distributional concerns.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or complex models into smaller, faster, or more constrained students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher. Over the past decade this has produced a diverse set of recipes — from logits/soft-label supervision to feature and layer-wise matching, progressive module replacement, data-free or privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/online variants — that together address deployment, privacy, robustness, and resource heterogeneity. Empirical work demonstrates that distilled students can approach teacher performance in NLP and vision tasks while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, or operation on weak devices; theoretical and empirical analyses illuminate when soft labels help, when hard labels or sample selection are needed, and how augmentation or task-aware selection of teacher knowledge improves transfer. Remaining challenges include principled understanding of which teacher signals are most useful for a given target task and resource constraint, robust and private distillation without original data, and scalable distillation in large distributed training regimes.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic into a practical, multi-purpose toolkit for compressing large models while preserving performance across domains and modalities. KD enables deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices, supports domain adaptation, helps preserve privacy, and can be adapted to architectures ranging from transformers to GANs and GNNs. Complementary techniques — e.g., architectural replacement, data augmentation, multi-teacher schemes, and precision reduction — expand KD’s effectiveness. However, KD’s success depends on how knowledge is represented and transferred (logits, internal representations, relations) and on availability or synthesis of appropriate data. The balance of method and setting determines whether KD yields compact models that meet real-world constraints without unacceptable loss of fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD techniques span soft-label transfer, intermediate representation matching, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and ensemble guidance, and adaptations for constrained or distributed settings. When combined with careful pretraining, representation-aware losses, selective sample strategies, and attention to privacy or robustness requirements, KD enables practical deployment of high-quality models on resource-limited devices and in federated environments.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks—language understanding, retrieval, visual recognition, graph-based prediction, and data-limited or privacy-constrained settings—distillation enables latency- and resource-constrained deployment. However, straightforward distillation is not a panacea: distribution shifts, heterogeneity of data and models, and absence of training data expose weaknesses that require complementary techniques (e.g., internal representation matching, layer mapping, task-aware selection, generative replay). Combining these advances yields compressed models that are both accurate and robust for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Findings, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring useful predictive behavior or internal structure from one or more teachers. A rich set of KD approaches exists — from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate representation imitation, attention and feature alignment, adversarial and projector-based techniques, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free or federated variants — and these have been applied across NLP, vision, graph-structured data, multimodal models, and generative models. Empirical work shows KD often recovers much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher/student compatibility, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Important practical concerns include preserving rare-token behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher errors or biases, enabling privacy-preserving or data-free compression, and combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search).

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans algorithmic advances in teacher–student objectives, architecture-aware compression, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Practical work shows gains from combining KD with data augmentation, many-to-many layer mappings, and architecture search, while complementary efforts address data-free and privacy-preserving distillation. Remaining challenges include imperfect teachers, data heterogeneity, and adapting compression to task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.
