papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a central strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s predictive power. A variety of mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate feature imitation, layer- or module-level mappings, and architecture-aware search—enable trade-offs among accuracy, latency, model size, and privacy. Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary methods (pretraining of compact architectures, pruning/quantization, data augmentation, and privacy-preserving synthesis) and tailor choices to data availability, task constraints, and target hardware. Despite broad empirical success, open issues remain around transferring robustness and rare-token behavior, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and designing distillation pipelines that are robust under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic training trick into a unifying framework for producing compact, efficient models across vision, speech, and language tasks. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble consensus from larger teachers to smaller students, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, compute, and latency while largely preserving accuracy. Beyond plain size reduction, KD adapts to constraints that arise in real deployments — limited data or privacy-sensitive settings, heterogeneous architectures, and modality gaps — through techniques such as feature-level alignment, selective sampling, ensemble-to-single-model transfer, and data-free synthesis. As a practical bridge between research-scale architectures and deployable systems, KD complements other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and serves both as an efficiency accelerator and as a lever for robustness and domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from soft-label matching to a family of methods that include feature- and attention-level imitation, layer mapping and projection, multi-teacher and online schedules, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and quantization. Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, but its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and provenance, and careful design choices about which signals to transfer. Open challenges include handling distribution shift, preserving rare-class or rare-token behavior, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors or undesirable behaviors. This synthesis summarizes common methods, mechanisms, practical patterns, and outstanding limitations to guide researchers and practitioners applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD provides multiple channels of transferable information (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals) that, when combined with complementary techniques (architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, or data synthesis), produce compact models that retain much of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is context-dependent: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals and data, and attention to robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic into a practical, multi-purpose toolkit for compressing large models while preserving performance across domains and modalities. KD enables deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices, supports domain adaptation, helps preserve privacy, and can be adapted to architectures ranging from transformers to GANs and GNNs. Complementary techniques — e.g., architectural replacement, data augmentation, multi-teacher schemes, and precision reduction — expand KD’s effectiveness. However, KD’s success depends on how knowledge is represented and transferred (logits, internal representations, relations) and on availability or synthesis of appropriate data. The balance of method and setting determines whether KD yields compact models that meet real-world constraints without unacceptable loss of fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity models to smaller, deployable models. Across computer vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, KD has been used to reduce inference cost while retaining most of the teacher model's performance. Research has advanced along several complementary axes: (1) methods that shape what is transferred (logits, hidden representations, attention or task-specific signals), (2) how the transfer is performed (layer-wise, multi-teacher, adversarial or student-aware training), (3) strategies to cope with limited or no access to original training data, and (4) techniques that preserve privacy and improve training efficiency. These lines of work show that careful alignment of objectives, attention to capacity gaps between teacher and student, and tailoring distillation to task and data regimes are critical for effective compression. Remaining challenges include robust cross-domain transfer, principled selection of what to distill for a target task, and maintaining robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Challenges, and Empirical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a diverse set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Approaches extend beyond matching soft logits to include intermediate-feature mimicry, attention-driven layer alignment, many-to-many layer mapping, contrastive representation alignment, and task- or domain-aware search and adaptation. Empirical work shows KD is effective across modalities and tasks — from pre-trained language models and visual-linguistic systems to object detectors, recommender rankers, graph networks, and continual learning settings — but practical deployment requires addressing representation misalignment, task specificity, and catastrophic forgetting. This review synthesizes core strategies and key empirical findings to guide application and future research.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation: Task-adaptive, Privacy-aware, and Feature-centric Compression for Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are now essential tools to deploy large deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. When applied thoughtfully—adapting to task requirements, leveraging feature-level signals, and accounting for data availability—KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher's performance while improving inference speed, memory footprint, and interpretability. However, naive distillation can fail under data heterogeneity, limited data, or strong teacher–student mismatches; addressing these requires task-aware layer selection, multi-teacher strategies, and alternatives to standard logit matching. I argue that the most effective KD pipelines combine task-adaptive compression, feature-directed supervision, and methods that preserve privacy and robustness to limited data.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically effective approach to compress large deep models into smaller, faster students for deployment. When combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware choices about what and how to transfer, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. At the same time, careful attention to data availability, teacher–student mismatch, and domain shift is required to preserve robustness and rare or domain-specific behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large, high-performance models into smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Recent work spans many complementary strategies — logit/soft-target matching, feature and layer-wise distillation, structural and channel-level transformations, data-free generation of proxy inputs, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and task-aware filtering — and addresses practical concerns such as cross-domain transfer, limited compute, and maintaining task performance in NLP settings. Progress includes specialized algorithms for pre-trained language model compression, algorithmic and architectural enhancements that reduce capacity gaps, and theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Together these developments offer a toolkit for deploying compact models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive environments while preserving most of the original model performance.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression strategies have become central tools for shrinking large pretrained models into efficient deployable networks while preserving much of their performance. Methods range from transferring final-logit 'dark knowledge' to matching intermediate representations, attention maps, or feature distributions; from engineering compact student architectures to progressively replacing modules inside a single model. Applications span vision, speech, generative models, and NLP (including BERT compression and non-autoregressive translation), and extensions address scenarios with no access to original training data or heterogeneous, federated settings. Key trade-offs involve accuracy vs. size/latency, robustness and fairness, and the distributional assumptions needed for effective transfer. Important open problems include principled understanding of when and why distillation helps, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and reliably transferring robustness and inductive biases to small models.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied and practically effective set of methods for producing smaller, faster models from larger, high-capacity teachers. KD unifies a range of strategies—from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations and generating synthetic training data—and is commonly combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks, but success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, data and augmentation strategies, and handling of domain shift or limited-data settings. The literature identifies both methodological extensions (multi-teacher fusion, online distillation, meta-learned teachers, data-free schemes) and recurring challenges (optimization mismatch, rare-token fidelity, privacy-aware transfer) that structure ongoing research and practical guidance.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a practical, flexible pathway to compress large models into compact, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive power. When combined with complementary techniques (pre-training, layer alignment, architecture-aware design, and data strategies), KD produces efficient models suitable for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings across modalities. This paper argues that KD should be a primary tool in compression pipelines and provides concrete, evidence-based prescriptions and caveats for practitioners.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to reproduce useful behavior of larger teacher models so that deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints becomes practical. KD encompasses a family of techniques — from matching teacher output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure — and is commonly combined with complementary compressions such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows that, when matched to student capacity and data availability, distilled students can approach teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Practical success depends on choices about which signals to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data access (including data-free alternatives), and robustness or fairness requirements; remaining challenges concern principled objective design, optimization under capacity mismatch, and reliable transfer of robustness and rare-token/long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a primary, flexible strategy for compressing large deep models into compact students that meet deployment constraints in deep learning and NLP. KD supports a wide range of supervision signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational losses), training protocols (offline, online, multi-teacher, adversarial, data-free), and combinations with structural compression (pruning, quantization) or architecture search. When applied with task- and student-aware design choices, KD delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs; however, its success depends on teacher quality, data availability, capacity alignment, and careful selection of what to transfer. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as the backbone of compression while integrating complementary methods and safeguards to address gaps in robustness, privacy, and out-of-distribution generalization.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications (Synthesis)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to emulate larger teacher models so that inference cost and storage are reduced while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD has evolved from soft-label transfer to a family of methods that include intermediate-feature matching, task-aware layer mapping, data-free and federated variants, and attention- or instance-aware strategies. Empirical work demonstrates KD’s practical value for deploying resource-constrained models, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. This synthesis summarizes prevailing approaches, practical patterns, application domains, and recurring limitations to guide future use and research.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: The Practical Foundations and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their accuracy. Its success arises from multiple complementary mechanisms—soft-target regularization, internal representation transfer, and architectural or data-side adaptations—that together explain why KD works across modalities (vision, language, graphs) and tasks (classification, QA, generation). However, KD is not a silver bullet: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, data properties (including augmentation and low-frequency phenomena), and deployment constraints such as federated or heterogeneous environments. Recognizing these mechanisms and limitations enables principled choices (e.g., teacher design, feature/projector choices, multi-teacher or adversarial schemes, and data strategies) to get the best trade-offs between compression and performance.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A diverse set of KD mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, attention- and relation-based signals, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data synthesis—has been developed and combined with structural compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance in many vision and language tasks, while remaining sensitive to teacher–student compatibility, data availability, domain shift, and robustness concerns. Practical pipelines therefore co-design student architectures, distillation targets, and data handling strategies to achieve the best trade-offs for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, high-impact approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD succeeds because it can transfer diverse forms of information—soft outputs, internal representations, relational structure—and because it composes naturally with complementary techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization, data augmentation, and multi-teacher ensembles). When applied with attention to teacher quality, data alignment, and student pretraining, KD enables practical, resource-aware deployments across vision, speech, and language tasks. This paper argues KD should often be the first method considered for compression, and outlines core mechanisms, practical recipes, and remaining challenges for robust application in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. A broad family of KD methods transfers teacher behavior through soft-label matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention- or task-aware layer projection, ensemble/online schemes, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols. When combined with architecture search, progressive module replacement, or data synthesis, KD enables strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs that make large pretrained models practical for edge, federated, and privacy-sensitive deployments. Key practical decisions include what form of knowledge to transfer, how to align mismatched teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or no access to original training data. Remaining challenges center on teacher–student compatibility, data heterogeneity, robustness under compression, and principled selection of distilled signals for downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Central, but Context‑Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their predictive power. KD methods span soft‑label/ logits transfer, intermediate‑feature and attention matching, adversarial and data‑free approaches, and teacher‑student co‑training or meta‑learned teachers. When thoughtfully designed — selecting appropriate distillation targets, aligning teacher and student capacities, and addressing data availability and robustness requirements — KD enables practical deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity constraints. However, KD is not universally successful: its effectiveness depends on architecture compatibility, quality and coverage of data (or of synthetic surrogates), and task‑specific choices, so practitioners must evaluate distillation under realistic conditions and adopt best practices tailored to their constraints.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used strategy for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from a teacher to a student. Across vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks KD variants—matching softened logits, aligning intermediate features or attention patterns, multi-teacher and progressive schemes, and self-distillation—have enabled compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Practical success typically requires co-design of the distillation signal, student architecture, data and augmentation choices, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., quantization or pruning). Persistent challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, handling limited or private data, preserving rare-token and robustness properties, and automating trade-offs between efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are a widely adopted toolkit for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the accuracy of larger teachers. Research across vision and language characterizes KD as a family of methods—transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training signals via specialized curricula or online exchanges—and shows that KD integrates naturally with pretraining, architecture design, and deployment-aware strategies. Practical success depends on matching the choice of knowledge (what to transfer), the teacher-student pairing (capacity and architecture), available data (real, augmented, or synthetic), and optimization curricula to the target task and constraints. While KD routinely yields substantial runtime and memory gains with modest accuracy loss, open challenges remain in handling domain shift, rare-token transfer in NLP, optimization mismatch, and large-scale or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. Practitioners apply KD not only as a logits-matching loss but as a system-level design primitive that includes representation matching, multi-teacher fusion, data and curriculum design, and combination with pruning and quantization. Its empirical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, relational signals), how to map teacher signals to potentially heterogeneous students, and how to handle limited or private data. While KD often yields compact models with near-teacher performance and useful regularization effects, limitations remain: imperfect teacher signals, optimization challenges, robustness and fairness transfer, and domain-shift or data-scarce scenarios. Current best practices emphasize task-aware selection of distilled signals, layer/projector alignment, and hybrid pipelines that combine KD with other compression techniques to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Tool: Compression, Transfer, and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) began as a model compression technique but has evolved into a flexible framework that accomplishes compression, regularization, domain adaptation, continual learning, fairness mitigation, and inductive-bias transfer across architectures and modalities. By choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations, or module behavior) and how to weight multi-source supervision, practitioners can adapt KD to the constraints and objectives of specific tasks. This paper argues that KD should be treated not merely as a compression trick but as a general-purpose mechanism for shaping student models, and it synthesizes empirical and theoretical evidence to recommend practical best practices for applying KD across modern deep learning and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When combined with representation-level objectives, architecture-aware techniques, and deployment-aware protocols, KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling real-world constraints such as latency, memory, and device heterogeneity to be met. Best practices include selecting appropriate distilled signals (beyond soft labels), pretraining or warming students, and aligning objectives with deployment constraints. Despite strong empirical success across modalities, open challenges remain in handling data heterogeneity, domain shift, privacy-sensitive settings, and the automated design of student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students that preserve most of the teacher’s capability. When treated as a toolkit rather than a single loss function, KD supports multiple forms of transferred knowledge (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational signals), and it interoperates with complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization) and data strategies (data-free synthesis, synthetic/distilled training sets). However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and quality, and explicit choices about what to transfer and how to align representations. Practitioners should therefore adopt KD as a first-line method while designing task- and deployment-aware distillation pipelines and monitoring known failure modes such as teacher error propagation, low-frequency token degradation, and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used approach to compress large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Research shows KD is a flexible toolkit: it can transfer final outputs (soft logits), intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and can be combined with architectural compression (pruning, quantization) or training strategies (online distillation, multi-teacher schedules). Empirical successes span classification, retrieval, reading comprehension, and large-scale language modeling, but outcomes depend strongly on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data availability, and optimization design. Important open problems include data-free distillation, cross-domain generalization, robustness and fairness preservation, and automated co-design of teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from larger, richer teacher models to smaller, cheaper student models to enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature encompasses simple soft-label matching, richer supervision signals that align intermediate features or attention, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-preserving designs, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and layer skipping. Empirical and theoretical work shows distillation can both compress and regularize models, but effectiveness depends on teacher-student mismatch, data availability, and optimization choices; practical pipelines therefore combine multiple compression mechanisms, careful signal selection, and task-aware adaptations.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Methods, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or aggregated multi-teacher signals—KD enables compact models that retain much of teacher performance while supporting complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware changes). KD also adapts to constrained settings (limited or private data, domain-specialization, federated or black-box teachers) but requires careful design choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and training curricula. When applied as part of a principled compression pipeline, KD offers a practical route to deployable high-quality models, though open problems remain in preserving rare-token behaviors, robustness, and reliable operation under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for converting large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision and NLP, KD produces favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with careful choices of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. However, KD’s effectiveness is context-dependent: teacher quality, capacity mismatch, data availability, and deployment constraints determine whether distilled students approach teacher performance or inherit undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their accuracy and desirable properties. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure) and in how and when the transfer occurs (offline teacher-to-student, online/co-distillation, adversarial/ensemble-driven, or data-free with synthetic samples). Across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks, KD is routinely combined with architecture-aware choices and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and domain-adaptation constraints. Empirical work shows strong gains in efficiency, but also highlights limitations: dependence on teacher quality and data alignment, possible degradation under domain shift or when sensitive attributes are transferred, and open problems in data-free or privacy-preserving settings. This synthesis summarizes key mechanisms, representative variants, cross-modal applications, common engineering practices, and the principal open challenges informed by recent empirical and survey literature.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to emulate larger teacher models so deployments meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD encompasses a spectrum of signals to transfer—including softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure—and integrates with pruning, quantization, and architecture design to produce efficient models. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often preserves large portions of teacher performance and can improve student generalization beyond mere compression, but outcomes depend strongly on what is distilled, teacher–student compatibility, access to data, and optimization choices. Practical pipelines therefore combine signal design, data strategies, and task-aware architecture choices to balance efficiency, robustness, and retained performance; open problems remain in data-free and privacy-preserving distillation, principled teacher design, and reliably transferring robustness and rare-token fidelity in sequence tasks.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable, empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s effectiveness. When treated as a flexible toolkit rather than a single loss, KD supports a range of transfer targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps), training regimes (single- and multi-teacher, online, data-free), and integrations with complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, access to appropriate data (or metadata), and careful choice of what and how to transfer. Best practice treats distillation as part of an end-to-end compression pipeline that explicitly addresses alignment, data constraints, and downstream task objectives.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad family of KD techniques—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, using multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and synthesizing data when originals are unavailable—has proven effective across vision, language, and other modalities. Practical success depends on co-designing what is transferred, student architecture and capacity, and data strategies; important open problems include robust transfer under domain shift, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, data-free and privacy-sensitive distillation, and principled combinations of KD with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and distributed settings KD often recovers much of a teacher's predictive performance while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, and deployment under resource or privacy constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: outcomes depend on what signals are transferred (logits, features, attention), teacher–student compatibility, availability and quality of data (including data-free or federated setups), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Best practice treats distillation as one element of a compression pipeline that combines representation matching, architecture-aware student design, data strategies, and risk-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Merritt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully — choosing what to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps), aligning teacher and student capacity, and addressing data constraints — KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and NLP tasks. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student architecture alignment, availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and explicit safeguards for robustness and fairness. Combining KD with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, data augmentation, and privacy-aware protocols) and adopting task-adaptive distillation pipelines yields the most reliable real-world outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of methods for transferring knowledge from larger, more expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so that the students retain much of the teachers' performance while meeting resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD methods include matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations or attention, synthesizing surrogate training data when original data are unavailable, and deploying progressive or ensemble-based strategies. Practical pipelines commonly combine KD with architecture-aware compression (pruning, quantization, or search) and training-time strategies (curricula, online distillation, or federated protocols) to balance efficiency and accuracy. Despite strong empirical success across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, open challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, operating under limited or private data, and designing principled objectives and curricula that preserve robustness and task-specific inductive biases.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from one or more high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple softened-logit matching into a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, relation-aware losses, layer-mapping strategies for large pretrained transformers, self-distillation, curriculum-driven distillation, and complementary use with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs and enables deployment under stringent latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its success depends on careful selection of distilled signals, teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and mitigation of optimization, robustness, and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of their predictive performance. Across modalities and tasks, practitioners use KD to achieve lower latency, smaller memory footprints, and easier deployment under resource, privacy, or heterogeneity constraints. Effective distillation combines choices about which knowledge to transfer (logits, features, attention maps), how to align teacher and student layers, how to generate or select training data, and how to adapt architectures to task requirements. While KD often succeeds when paired with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture search, ensembling, data augmentation), its effectiveness depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and quality, and targeted objectives that reflect downstream tasks. Recognizing the mechanisms and limits of KD helps practitioners design robust compression pipelines that balance efficiency, accuracy, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, Practical Outcomes, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, ensembling or progressive teacher schedules, and operating under data constraints (including data-free or synthetic-data strategies). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and student-aware design, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, data provenance and availability, and training protocols; KD can propagate teacher errors (particularly for rare tokens/classes), degrade under distribution shift, and incur extra training overhead unless efficiency techniques are applied. Best practice treats KD as a flexible pipeline: choose appropriate distillation targets, reconcile architectural mismatches, use data strategies that match deployment constraints, and combine KD with other compression and robustness-aware methods.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher(s) to student(s). Advances span logit- and feature-based matching, multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, data-free and federated scenarios, and domain- or task-specific adaptations in NLP. Practical work shows KD can yield large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but design choices (what to match, how to weight teachers, whether data are available, and deployment constraints) strongly affect outcomes. Remaining challenges include robustness to domain shift, privacy and communication constraints in distributed settings, and principled handling of teacher–student mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large, high-performance models into smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Recent work spans many complementary strategies — logit/soft-target matching, feature and layer-wise distillation, structural and channel-level transformations, data-free generation of proxy inputs, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and task-aware filtering — and addresses practical concerns such as cross-domain transfer, limited compute, and maintaining task performance in NLP settings. Progress includes specialized algorithms for pre-trained language model compression, algorithmic and architectural enhancements that reduce capacity gaps, and theoretical analyses that clarify when and why distillation helps. Together these developments offer a toolkit for deploying compact models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive environments while preserving most of the original model performance.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Complementary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical, flexible route to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher’s capability. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, variants of KD — including multi-teacher schemes, internal-representation matching, self-distillation, many-to-many layer mapping, and data-free approaches — have shown that distilled students can approach or even match teacher performance. KD is also complementary to pruning and quantization, enabling stacked compression pipelines that meet strict hardware constraints. I argue KD should be a first-line technique for model compression in deep learning and NLP, applied in combination with other resource-aware methods and chosen variants adapted to data availability and task structure.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) refers to a family of techniques that transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost and memory while retaining much of the teacher performance. KD spans simple soft-target (logit) matching to richer objectives that align intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure, or representation geometry, and it is combined in practice with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Practical deployments show KD is broadly effective across vision, graph, and language tasks, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability (including data-free regimes), and the specific design of distillation signals and training curricula.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) transfer into a broad toolkit that also includes intermediate representation matching, attention- and layer-aware objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and combinations with structural compression. Practical deployments of KD require careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, and how to handle limited or no access to original training data. While KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss in many settings, open problems remain in robustness under distribution shift, privacy- and data-constrained regimes, and principled selection of distilled signals for downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students that retain much of the teacher's performance. Across NLP, vision, and generative models, KD takes many forms (soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention alignment, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher schemes, and data-free synthesis) and is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving accuracy under many conditions, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and optimization protocols. Practical deployment requires careful design choices and remains an active area for research on robustness, rare-token preservation, privacy, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for compressing large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students that retain much of the teachers' performance. Modern KD extends beyond soft-label matching to include representation-level objectives, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-free or zero-shot variants, and architecture-aware combinations with pruning, quantization, and search. KD has been applied successfully across domains — including language generation, ranking, detection, and federated settings — but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to manage data, privacy, and distributional shift. Practical deployment requires selecting distillation signals and training regimes that match student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students that are suitable for deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. A spectrum of KD techniques—from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations, multi-teacher supervision, and architecture-aware student design—has been shown to recover much of teacher performance when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical success depends on choices of distillation signal, data availability and alignment between teacher and student; practical systems also require attention to computational cost during distillation and to domain or heterogeneity challenges in distributed settings. Remaining gaps include principled selection of teacher signals for specific tasks, reliable data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and methods that scale distillation quality and efficiency simultaneously.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The method encompasses supervising students with softened teacher outputs as well as transferring intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful choices about data, teacher–student alignment, and optimization protocols, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Important open challenges include handling data-poor or data-free settings, mitigating transfer of undesirable behaviors (bias, privacy leakage), and reliably transferring rare or fine-grained knowledge across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level Primitive for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. When treated as a system-level primitive rather than a single loss term, KD can be adapted to data availability, deployment constraints, and student–teacher mismatch to produce compact models that retain much of teachers' performance. Practical application of KD involves choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relational signals), how to expose students to informative inputs (real, synthesized, or online predictions), and how to combine KD with complementary compression methods and privacy-preserving protocols. Despite strong empirical success, KD has known failure modes tied to teacher errors, limited data, and distribution shift that require targeted mitigations and principled design.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical First-Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed as a system-level technique—choosing what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data constraints—KD routinely produces compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. Practical KD pipelines combine diverse signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps), data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation), and complementary compression steps (progressive module replacement, pruning, quantization) to address domain shifts and deployment constraints. Despite limitations related to teacher–student mismatch and optimization challenges, KD's adaptability across tasks and ability to incorporate robustness and data-free methods make it the recommended primary approach for real-world model compression.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or complex models into smaller, faster, or more constrained students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher. Over the past decade this has produced a diverse set of recipes — from logits/soft-label supervision to feature and layer-wise matching, progressive module replacement, data-free or privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/online variants — that together address deployment, privacy, robustness, and resource heterogeneity. Empirical work demonstrates that distilled students can approach teacher performance in NLP and vision tasks while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, or operation on weak devices; theoretical and empirical analyses illuminate when soft labels help, when hard labels or sample selection are needed, and how augmentation or task-aware selection of teacher knowledge improves transfer. Remaining challenges include principled understanding of which teacher signals are most useful for a given target task and resource constraint, robust and private distillation without original data, and scalable distillation in large distributed training regimes.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a unifying, practical framework to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable students while addressing concerns of computation, privacy, robustness, and limited task data. KD techniques span from logits- and feature-based matching to progressive module replacement, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free (zero-shot) synthesis, and federated output-sharing, and when combined with careful data augmentation and generative replay they yield compact models that retain much of the teacher utility in real-world settings.
