papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and natural language processing. The family of KD methods spans soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate representation and attention imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble-derived strategies, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and online or co-distillation schemes. Successful application requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, whether original data are available (or must be synthesized), and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical practice shows KD frequently yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but open problems remain around robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, theoretical understanding of transfer dynamics, and scalable private or data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad family of KD techniques—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, using multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and synthesizing data when originals are unavailable—has proven effective across vision, language, and other modalities. Practical success depends on co-designing what is transferred, student architecture and capacity, and data strategies; important open problems include robust transfer under domain shift, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, data-free and privacy-sensitive distillation, and principled combinations of KD with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or complex models into smaller, faster, or more constrained students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher. Over the past decade this has produced a diverse set of recipes — from logits/soft-label supervision to feature and layer-wise matching, progressive module replacement, data-free or privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/online variants — that together address deployment, privacy, robustness, and resource heterogeneity. Empirical work demonstrates that distilled students can approach teacher performance in NLP and vision tasks while enabling faster inference, lower memory use, or operation on weak devices; theoretical and empirical analyses illuminate when soft labels help, when hard labels or sample selection are needed, and how augmentation or task-aware selection of teacher knowledge improves transfer. Remaining challenges include principled understanding of which teacher signals are most useful for a given target task and resource constraint, robust and private distillation without original data, and scalable distillation in large distributed training regimes.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing deep models while preserving or even improving performance. Beyond the canonical soft-target distillation, variants that transfer internal representations, mimic features, adapt across modalities, and incorporate adversarial or online strategies make KD effective for many real-world constraints: limited compute, privacy/no-data settings, robustness requirements, ensemble compression, and large-scale distributed training. When applied thoughtfully—choosing the appropriate supervision signal (logits, features, attentions), architecture adapters (projectors), and training protocol (adversarial, online, or teacher-free)—distillation yields compact models that meet deployment constraints without sacrificing task performance.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has grown from matching softened output distributions to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data-free/zero-shot synthesis, and architecture-aware co-design. Empirical work demonstrates KD's ability to reduce parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks; its practical success depends on careful choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to manage data and augmentation. Remaining challenges include robust distillation under domain shift, preserving rare-token behavior in language models, privacy-sensitive settings, and principled combination of KD with other compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable family of techniques that transfer information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving predictive performance. KD methods differ in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational structure) and how training proceeds (offline teacher supervision, online/co-distillation, self-distillation, or data-free synthesis). Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and require attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability, and task-specific choices. Empirical evidence shows KD reliably yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, but success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signals, and constraints such as access to original training data or deployment hardware.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used family of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD encompasses logit-level soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational or ensemble signals, and many practical variants (online, self-distillation, data-free). When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student co-design, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for classification, sequence tasks, retrieval, and generative systems. However, KD is not universally effective: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and distributional match, and the choice of distillation signals; open problems include reliable distillation without original data, preserving low-frequency or rare behaviors in NLP, and avoiding transfer of undesirable properties such as biases or fragility.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural teachers into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, KD techniques include soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention- or relation-based alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher fusion, and data- or domain-aware variations. Empirical work shows that distilled students often recover most teacher performance and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design to meet deployment constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and training objectives. Remaining challenges include reliable distillation without original data, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behavior, transferring robustness and inductive biases, and handling heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive environments.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students that retain much of the teacher's performance. Across NLP, vision, and generative models, KD takes many forms (soft-target matching, intermediate-feature imitation, attention alignment, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher schemes, and data-free synthesis) and is often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving accuracy under many conditions, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher–student compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and optimization protocols. Practical deployment requires careful design choices and remains an active area for research on robustness, rare-token preservation, privacy, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to reproduce useful behavior of larger teacher models so that deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints becomes practical. KD encompasses a family of techniques — from matching teacher output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure — and is commonly combined with complementary compressions such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows that, when matched to student capacity and data availability, distilled students can approach teacher performance across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Practical success depends on choices about which signals to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, data access (including data-free alternatives), and robustness or fairness requirements; remaining challenges concern principled objective design, optimization under capacity mismatch, and reliable transfer of robustness and rare-token/long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass methods that transfer information from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, deployable models (students), or otherwise reduce network size while retaining performance. Approaches range from matching final predictions to aligning intermediate representations, and they address practical constraints such as limited data, privacy, device heterogeneity, and robustness. Recent work spans algorithmic mechanisms (soft targets, layer mapping, adversarial sample synthesis), application-specific pipelines (BERT compression, non-autoregressive translation, task-adaptive models), and theoretical interpretations that link distillation to regularization. This synthesis summarizes core techniques, practical extensions, and open challenges reported in recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the First-Line, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated approach for converting large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Treated as a toolkit rather than a single loss, KD supports multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free), and integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). I argue KD should serve as the first-line strategy for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP pipelines, provided practitioners adopt principled, context-aware distillation recipes and pair KD with targeted validation for robustness and distributional concerns.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Multifaceted, and Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical mechanism for turning large, expensive models into smaller, deployable ones while often preserving much of their predictive quality. KD serves multiple roles beyond pure compression — it regularizes learning, enables domain adaptation, supports heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive deployments, and can be adapted at the logit, feature, or data level. However, its success depends on teacher quality, the form of transferred knowledge, data properties (including low-frequency phenomena), and deployment constraints; KD is therefore a powerful but not universally sufficient tool. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a design paradigm with principled choices (what to transfer, how to adapt teachers, how to combine data and synthetic targets, and how to handle heterogeneity) rather than a one-size-fits-all recipe, and it outlines practical recommendations for applying KD across vision and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. Practitioners apply KD not only as a logits-matching loss but as a system-level design primitive that includes representation matching, multi-teacher fusion, data and curriculum design, and combination with pruning and quantization. Its empirical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, relational signals), how to map teacher signals to potentially heterogeneous students, and how to handle limited or private data. While KD often yields compact models with near-teacher performance and useful regularization effects, limitations remain: imperfect teacher signals, optimization challenges, robustness and fairness transfer, and domain-shift or data-scarce scenarios. Current best practices emphasize task-aware selection of distilled signals, layer/projector alignment, and hybrid pipelines that combine KD with other compression techniques to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Insufficient Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach for converting large neural teachers into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when applied thoughtfully, but it is not a standalone solution: real-world compression requires attention to what is transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data provenance and availability, robustness and safety concerns, and the coordinated use of complementary compression methods such as architecture search, pruning, and curriculum or data strategies. Treating KD as a system-level primitive and combining it with targeted interventions produces the most reliable, efficient, and robust compressed models for production NLP and deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical paradigm for compressing and accelerating large deep models by transferring information from a cumbersome teacher to a compact student. Across modalities and tasks—supervised classification, representation learning, structured prediction, and generation—research shows KD can produce lightweight models that approach teacher performance, recover performance of small architectures, or enable new deployment constraints (privacy, federated settings). However, success depends critically on what is distilled (outputs, intermediate representations, attention across layers), the data or metadata available for distillation, and the learning dynamics between teacher and student. Open challenges include optimization barriers that prevent exact teacher matching, sensitivity to data heterogeneity, and designing teachers or distillation procedures that reliably transfer the right kind of knowledge for a target student capacity and deployment setting.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, often over-parameterized teacher models into smaller, more efficient students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD strategies vary in what is transferred (soft targets, intermediate representations, relations), how it is transferred (logit matching, feature-mimicking, projector layers, contrastive objectives, adversarial losses), and in deployment settings (data-available, data-free, federated or distributed, and online). Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, distilled students frequently recover much of teacher performance while enabling practical gains in speed and memory; however, method choice, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and distributional shifts materially affect outcomes, and open problems remain in preserving rare-token behavior, transferring robustness and fairness, and compressing across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for making large neural models deployable: by transferring richer supervision from high-capacity teacher models to compact students, KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often preserving or even improving generalization. Best results arise when distillation strategies are matched to deployment constraints and student capacity—combining logits and representational objectives, co-designing teacher and student, using appropriate data-augmentation or synthetic-data strategies, and integrating structural compression like pruning or module replacement. Although challenges remain (teacher imperfections, low-frequency token fidelity, data-free settings, and distribution shift), a set of practical, complementary methods yields robust pathways to efficient models across NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Challenges, and Empirical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a diverse set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Approaches extend beyond matching soft logits to include intermediate-feature mimicry, attention-driven layer alignment, many-to-many layer mapping, contrastive representation alignment, and task- or domain-aware search and adaptation. Empirical work shows KD is effective across modalities and tasks — from pre-trained language models and visual-linguistic systems to object detectors, recommender rankers, graph networks, and continual learning settings — but practical deployment requires addressing representation misalignment, task specificity, and catastrophic forgetting. This review synthesizes core strategies and key empirical findings to guide application and future research.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First-line, Context-aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to what knowledge is transferred, how intermediate layers are aligned, and whether data or privacy constraints hold, KD can yield compact models that retain much of teacher performance while enabling large gains in inference speed and memory. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: optimization difficulties, mismatches in capacity between teacher and student, and limited or private data require tailored objectives, architecture-aware choices, and complementary techniques. This essay argues KD should be a primary strategy in model-compression toolkits while recommending concrete practices to increase reliability across real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The approach spans logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, self-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and combinations with structural compression such as pruning and quantization. KD is effective across modalities and tasks but its empirical success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and training dynamics; open challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, robustness, privacy, and heterogeneous architecture transfer.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, practical toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and natural language processing. The family of KD methods spans soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate representation and attention imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble-derived strategies, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and online or co-distillation schemes. Successful application requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, whether original data are available (or must be synthesized), and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical practice shows KD frequently yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but open problems remain around robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, theoretical understanding of transfer dynamics, and scalable private or data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost while retaining performance. A broad family of approaches—from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature imitation, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free synthesis, and federated or privacy-aware protocols—enables deployment across vision, speech, and language tasks. Practical success depends on matching the distillation signal to student capacity, combining KD with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, pretraining), and addressing data, optimization, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile family of techniques for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across vision and language, KD variants—ranging from softened-logit transfer to intermediate-feature mimicry, attention matching, adversarial and data-free synthesis, and task-aware architecture search—enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and applied with careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data handling, and training curricula, KD routinely delivers large reductions in model size and inference cost while keeping accuracy losses modest. Nonetheless, KD is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on the choice of transferred signals, training data availability, teacher quality, and explicit checks for robustness and distribution shift. Practical adoption requires co-design of teacher and student, selection of appropriate distillation objectives, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from one or more high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple softened-logit matching into a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, relation-aware losses, layer-mapping strategies for large pretrained transformers, self-distillation, curriculum-driven distillation, and complementary use with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs and enables deployment under stringent latency, memory, and privacy constraints, its success depends on careful selection of distilled signals, teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and mitigation of optimization, robustness, and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, insights, and practical trends
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in latency-, memory-, and compute-constrained settings. Work across speech, NLP, vision, and graph domains demonstrates a spectrum of approaches: matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate features, progressively replacing modules, augmenting or synthesizing training data for better student generalization, and compressing ensembles into single models. Empirical results show substantial speed and size gains with modest accuracy loss when methods are carefully matched to task and architecture. Important themes include (1) the role of dark/soft labels vs. intermediate feature signals, (2) architectural or task-aware compression (including search), (3) techniques that increase the student’s exposure to informative training points (e.g., mixup or adversarial examples), and (4) distillation strategies tailored for ensembles or heterogeneous teacher–student pairs. Open challenges remain in principled sample selection, robust transfer of inductive biases, and automated trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single teacher→student soft-label transfer into a broad toolkit for compressing and adapting deep models across vision, language, and multimodal domains. Contemporary approaches extend logits matching to representation- and structure-aware objectives, multi- and continual-teaching schemes, task-aware layer selection, and combinations with pruning or architecture-level compression. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints but its success depends on design choices about what is transferred, how the student is supervised, data availability, and student capacity. Practical progress emphasizes representation matching beyond logits, careful layer- and channel-level alignment, and composing KD with other compression techniques; remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, data-free scenarios, and preserving fine-grained or safety-critical behavior.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD variants transfer information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and adversarially or synthetically generated inputs. When combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, or data strategies, KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, success depends on careful matching of what is transferred to student capacity, handling data scarcity or distribution shift, and mitigating propagation of teacher errors. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, representative algorithmic families, empirical patterns, and actionable recommendations for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models into smaller, more deployable student models. KD methods operate at multiple levels — output logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure — and are commonly combined with architecture-level compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and training strategies (online co-training, curriculum schedules, synthetic-data protocols). Empirical evidence across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while improving latency and memory usage, but success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and appropriate choice of transfer signal. Ongoing challenges include robust transfer under distribution shift, aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, and operating in data-limited or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models or ensembles into smaller, efficient student models. KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, multi-teacher or online schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants; they are frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical results across vision, speech, language, generative, and 3D tasks show that distilled students can recover much of teacher performance when distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, and data strategies are chosen appropriately, but open problems remain around data-free scenarios, robustness to distribution shift, fairness, and automated student design.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of methods that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models so deployments meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate-representation and attention matching, relational or structural transfer, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-side interventions (including data-free and few-shot protocols). When combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and appropriate data and optimization practices, KD yields compact models that recover a large fraction of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. Open problems include principled theory of when KD helps, reliably transferring robustness and fairness, handling distribution shift and rare or low-frequency phenomena in NLP, and automated student design under strict resource budgets.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Backbone with Bounded Limits for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted, practical strategy for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels and, when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression techniques, yields efficient models suitable for latency- and memory-constrained deployments. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and objective design, and practitioners must address robustness, fairness, and task-specific constraints to realize reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied model compression technique that trains a compact student model to emulate a larger teacher (or ensemble) so that inference cost and storage are reduced while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD has been adapted across domains (vision, graphs, NLP, multimodal systems) and combined with other compression methods; it can transfer logits, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge, and it can be extended to multi-teacher, self-distillation, and privacy-aware settings. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often improves generalization but also reveals limits and failure modes that motivate augmented objectives, data strategies, and teacher-training methods to achieve more effective, fair, and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods for transferring behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment under resource constraints. Rather than a single algorithm, KD comprises multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational losses) and training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free) that should be chosen to match student capacity, data availability, and downstream requirements. Effective compression usually combines KD with complementary techniques (pretraining, pruning, quantization) and careful alignment between teacher and student. Practical success thus depends on design choices and trade-offs rather than a universal distillation recipe.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context‑Dependent Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

Real-world success requires representation-aware objectives, options for data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings, and careful evaluation under distribution shift and modality-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical First‑Line Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Promise, Mechanisms, and Responsible Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, practically effective approach for producing compact models that can be deployed under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. When treated as a flexible design paradigm rather than a single loss, KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals), integrates with complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization), and adapts to task- and data-specific constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher quality and compatibility, the choice of distilled signals, data availability (including data-free or synthetic strategies), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and low-frequency behavior. A considered KD pipeline—combining softened logits, representational guidance, task-aware objectives, architecture-aware search, and careful data strategies—yields compact students that meet real-world deployment needs while mitigating common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and pragmatic approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer predictive behavior and internal representations, and—when co-designed with architecture choices, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques—routinely yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability and provenance, token- or class-level coverage in the teacher, and careful handling of optimization dynamics and robustness. I argue that KD should be treated as a central, system-level tool for model compression in deep learning and NLP, used together with targeted engineering and auditing to manage its limits and to maximize practical benefit.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation: Practical, Theoretical, and Methodological Evidence for Efficient Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and mature approach for producing smaller, faster, and more deployable models by transferring information from richer teacher models to compact students. Across modalities and tasks—NLP, vision, graph learning, and retrieval—KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while retaining most of the teacher's performance. Beyond pure compression, KD variants address practical deployment concerns: multi-teacher and confidence-aware schemes improve robustness to imperfect teachers; progressive and module-level replacement approaches enable deeper integrated compression; online/distillation-in-parallel techniques scale training and improve reproducibility; and targeted feature-distillation methods refine representational quality. Theory of wide networks provides guidance on when soft labels help and when mixing hard labels is beneficial. Together, empirical and theoretical work shows KD is a versatile, well-grounded toolbox for model compression and knowledge transfer in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Donovan

Realistic deployment requires combining KD with complementary compression techniques, adapting the distillation signal to the task and student capacity, and evaluating robustness and privacy implications.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the original performance. KD has proven effective across modalities and tasks, and modern practice extends beyond simple logit matching to include intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher fusion, data-free approaches, and training-time strategies that make teachers more amenable to transfer. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all solution: distribution shifts, limited or absent training data, teacher–student mismatch, and adversarial concerns require complementary techniques and careful design. When combined with task-aware selection of distilled signals, student-friendly teacher training, and data- or representation-aware remedies, KD becomes a practical backbone for deployment under latency, compute, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Practical compression typically combines KD with architecture-aware design, pretraining, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, or layer skipping). Success depends on careful matching of distilled signals to the student architecture and deployment constraints; important open problems include handling teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift and heterogeneity, preserving rare or low-frequency information, and maintaining robustness and privacy in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. KD has been applied successfully to compress large language models, vision transformers, and task-specific architectures, and adapted to settings including self-supervision, multi-task learning, and privacy-sensitive or data-limited regimes. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on the alignment between teacher and student architectures, the availability and quality of data (or of synthetic surrogates), the selection of what knowledge to transfer (logits, features, attention, relational signals), and task-specific choices such as layer-wise matching and curriculum. Recognizing both the demonstrated strengths and the practical failure modes of KD leads to targeted best practices: choose distillation targets that match the student capacity and task, use task-aware or feature-focused objectives for intermediate representations, apply adversarial or synthetic data approaches when original data are unavailable, and explicitly evaluate KD under realistic heterogeneity (e.g., federated or multi-task) to avoid hidden degradations.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a First‑Line, Context‑Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical and flexible pathway to convert large, high‑performing models into compact students suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When matched to student capacity and task constraints, distillation can preserve most of a teacher’s performance while enabling complementary compression (quantization, pruning) and deployment strategies. Realistic application of KD requires attention to what signals are transferred (logits, intermediate features, attention, or relational structure), how teacher and student inputs and architectures are aligned, and how limited or synthetic data are used. KD also carries risks—propagation of teacher errors, loss of rare‑token behavior, domain shift sensitivity, and privacy issues—that mandate task‑aware design and evaluation.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad toolkit—logit-level supervision, intermediate-feature matching, layer-mapping, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants—has been developed to meet deployment constraints in vision and natural language tasks. Empirical work shows that, when combined with architecture-aware choices and complementary compression techniques, KD frequently yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, though careful method selection is required to mitigate mismatches, data limitations, and task-specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Primary Compression Strategy for Practical Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the first-line strategy for compressing large deep models into deployable students: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations, is broadly applicable across modalities, and composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is not a silver bullet — its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, data availability, and how knowledge is represented and aligned — so production pipelines should combine KD with representation-aware objectives, student pretraining, and targeted data strategies to mitigate distributional and optimization pitfalls. When applied with these caveats, KD delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs that make large pretrained models practical for constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-strategy approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods include transferring softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and data-free or few-shot variants to handle limited or private data. Best results come from treating KD as one element of a broader compression pipeline that also incorporates architecture-aware choices, data strategies, and explicit attention to robustness and fairness. KD is therefore a central tool for efficient deployment, but it has clear limits and must be designed carefully to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors or losing rare-token performance.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of teacher performance. Research across vision, speech, translation, and NLP tasks has developed multiple KD objectives (soft logits, intermediate-feature matching, attention or projector-based alignment), training regimes (offline teacher–student, self-distillation, multi-teacher, adversarial transfer), and data strategies (data-free, distilled datasets, and hybrid authentic/synthetic training). Empirical and theoretical work explains why KD often improves student generalization (dark-knowledge regularization, transferred inductive biases) while also documenting limitations (capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, distributional/low-frequency failures) and practical remedies. Best practice is to treat KD as a flexible toolkit and combine it with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD techniques span soft-label transfer, intermediate representation matching, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and ensemble guidance, and adaptations for constrained or distributed settings. When combined with careful pretraining, representation-aware losses, selective sample strategies, and attention to privacy or robustness requirements, KD enables practical deployment of high-quality models on resource-limited devices and in federated environments.

papers_seen.author: Salazar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models so that deployments meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD methods range from soft-logit matching to intermediate-feature and attention-level transfer, multi-teacher fusion, and data- or privacy-aware protocols. Its practical success depends strongly on teacher–student alignment, the choice of distilled signals, data availability (or plausible synthetic surrogates), and integration with complementary compression primitives such as pruning and quantization. KD is therefore best treated as a context-dependent component of compression pipelines rather than a single recipe; doing so enables robust, efficient models for a wide range of deep-learning and NLP applications while revealing clear directions for research on heterogeneity, rare-token behavior, and privacy-preserving transfer.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task-aware choices for what and how to transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), and when combined with complementary compression strategies (architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, data augmentation or synthesis), KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, teacher–student alignment, availability or synthesis of appropriate data, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy risks. Practical compression pipelines therefore treat distillation as a core tool whose design must be tailored to the deployment context.
